sections.Behavior:
Isaac lies on the ground in the middle of the room and does not begin attacking until he takes damage.

During all three of Isaac's phases, he continuously shoots multiple projectiles in the player's direction at fixed intervals when not performing other attacks. After taking enough damage, he begins to shoot double projectiles and triple projectiles.

=== Phase 1 ===
Isaac remains stationary on the ground and performs the following attacks:
* Shoots 10 lines of projectiles in every direction.
* Shoots 8 groups of projectiles that curve back towards him.
* Shoots 8 groups of long-range spinning projectiles along with 10 slightly curved lines of shorter-range projectiles in every direction.

=== Phase 2 ===
Isaac stands up but remains stationary and performs the following attack:
* Isaac alternates between two projectile patterns:
** Shoots 4 projectiles in a cross pattern, which splits into four short-ranged projectiles after a short time, similar to {{i|Cricket's Body}}.
** Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions.
Independently of his projectile attack:
* Summons {{e|Angelic Baby|text=Angelic Babies}} in a pair.
* Summons 2 {{i|Crack the Sky}} beams at random locations.

=== Phase 3 ===
Isaac grows a pair of angelic wings and is no longer stationary, moving towards where the player is predicted to go with short dashes. During which he also performs the following attacks:
* Teleports off-screen and summons {{i|Crack the Sky}} beams to cover the screen, starting from one of the top corners to the opposite bottom corner. After teleporting back on-screen, he shoots the 10 lines of projectiles from the first phase. He always performs this attack at the start of this phase and repeats this process every time he takes 200 damage.
** {{dlc|r}} Shadows indicate ahead of time where the beams strike.
* Can perform all projectile patterns from the first phase.

sections.Notes:
* Every time Isaac is defeated, the current [[Savefile Images|savefile's image]] changes until {{i|The Polaroid}} is unlocked.
* Isaac does not begin attacking until he has been damaged. This can be exploited to make the fight much easier by dealing large amounts of damage in the first hit. Methods of doing this include saving up a large amount of tears with {{I|Anti-Gravity}}, waiting for {{I|Kidney Stone}} to activate before shooting Isaac, or placing multiple bombs and detonating them all at once with {{I|Remote Detonator}}. {{I|Glass Cannon}} can also provide a high-damage initial shot, but doing this is extremely risky due to Glass Cannon's additional effect of reducing health to one half-heart.
** {{Dlc|r}}Glass Cannon no longer reduces health on use, so it can be used against Isaac much more effectively.

sections.Behavior:
Little Horn constantly tries to evade Isaac by moving away from him while performing the following attacks:
* Creates and jumps into a {{e|Pitfall}} and pops up elsewhere.
* Creates 3 to 5 {{e|Teleport Pitfall|text=Teleport Pitfalls}} that move outwards.
* Creates a regular Pitfall under himself that lasts for several seconds.
* Throws a {{e|Troll Bomb}} or a {{e|Mega Troll Bomb}} into a created Pitfall underneath himself. The bomb then pops up near Isaac's position.
* Jumps into a Pitfall and appears elsewhere while leaving a Troll Bomb in his place; repeats this process 3-5 times.
* Spawns a {{e|Dark Ball}}.
{{dlc|r}} Little Horn takes reduced damage (25 instead of 100) from his own bombs. Bombs from other sources still do full damage.
sections.Notes:
* The {{i|Gnawed Leaf}} can make the battle easier, as Little Horn will damage himself with his bombs over time. Isaac can still fall into the pits and be transported around the screen, and will ''appear'' to suffer damage, but no actual loss of HP will occur if he is in statue form when he falls in.
* The Dark Balls that Little Horn spawns can appear in [[Closets]] in the {{s|Caves}} and the {{s|Flooded Caves}}. They also appear in a room with Little Horn in the {{s|Chest}}.
* If Isaac has the {{t|Safety Scissors|n}}, he can acquire maximum bombs from the fight at fairly little risk since the bombs Little Horn spawns will turn into bomb pickups and all his hole attacks are easy to dodge.
* Little Horn's Dark Ball is considered a monster. Killing it will activate items such as {{i|Charm of the Vampire}}, {{i|Infestation 2}}, and {{i|Jar of Flies|n}}.
* Occasionally, a Pitfall that Little Horn summons will not vanish after defeating the boss. The Pitfall is still active and can damage Isaac, even if it does not actively chase the player.

sections.Behavior:
Daddy Long Legs' head hangs down stationary and can perform the following attacks:
* Raises his head, making it invulnerable, and stomps the ground in random locations around the room 4 times in quick succession. {{Dlc|r}} One of these legs will always stomp on top of Isaac's position.
** The appendages that he stomps with can be attacked to damage him.
* Lifts his head off-screen and stomps the ground 4 times at regular intervals on top of Isaac's position. At the end of the 4 stomps, he slams his head down quickly, shooting out 8 projectiles in all directions. He can only slam his head down along a horizontal plane across the center of the room and slams it down close to Isaac's position.
** Occasionally performs a fifth stomp before slamming his head down.
** The appendages that he stomps with can be attacked to damage him.
* Spits out 2-3 {{e|Spider}}s.
** These spiders can be killed by Daddy Long Legs' stomps and head slam.
Daddy Long Legs' foot stomp and head slam deal a whole heart of contact damage.
sections.Notes:

* On rooms where Daddy Long Legs is treated as a degraded Boss, they can be used to blow open doors.
* {{dlc|nr}} Like {{e|Mom}}'s stomp, his stomp deals explosive damage.

Carrion Queen is only vulnerable in the flesh segment of her behind. She moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:
* Carrion Queen charges at Isaac whenever he lines up with one of her cardinal directions.
** Like {{e|Chub}}, Carrion Queen eats any {{e|Bomb}}s dropped in her path; stunning her for a moment before dealing considerable damage.
* Spawns a damaging {{g|Red Poop}}, up to a maximum of 5.

* When below half health, Carrion Queen begins to move diagonally, similar to {{e|The Hollow}}, but without flight. She no longer performs her previous attacks from '''Phase 1'''.
** She will bounce off of obstacles and her own Red Poop damaging it and destroying it in the process.
Carrion Queen deals a whole heart of contact damage in both phases.

=== Phase 1 ===
Brownie remains stationary and performs the following attacks:
* Each time Brownie takes enough damage, he spawns a single {{e|Brownie Corn}}; if Brownie takes a lot of damage in a single instance, the Brownie Corns are spawned together in a group.
* Occasionally spawns a group 5-8 Brownie Corns upon taking damage.
** While moving during some attacks, he crushes any Brownie Corns in his path, regaining 3 HP for each.
* Farts, pushing away Isaac and knocking back any Brownie Corns if they are too close.
* Spins a short distance across the room, bouncing off walls and finishing with a fart.
** Sometimes leaves slippery [[brown creep]] and a {{e|Corn Mine}} in his path.
* Slides across the room, bouncing off walls, while leaving a trail of slippery Brown Creep, continuously spawning Corn Mines, and occasionally shooting corny projectiles towards Isaac. Finishes this attack with a fart.
** The Corn Mines' corn projectiles and gas can damage and poison Brownie. While poisoned, he leaves damaging [[green creep]] instead of Brown Creep.
* Twirls and jumps 4-6 times around the room, creating a puddle of Brown Creep every time he lands and tossing corny projectiles in random directions.
** Brownie can sometimes directly chain into this attack from his spinning and sliding attacks instead of finishing them with farts.
Brownie's expression when idle changes as he gets damaged by Isaac – going from happy to grumpy. This appears to have a correlation with how aggressive he is in performing attacks, chaining attacks, and how many corny projectiles are released in his attacks.

=== Phase 2 ===
* When Brownie reaches around 25% health, he degrades into a 75 HP {{e|Dangle}} that behaves regularly.
sections.Notes:
* Brownie may be paired along with regular {{e|Dip}}s in a Boss Room.
* If a {{i|Butt Bombs}} Bomb goes off in the same room as Brownie, it heals him.
** {{dlc|a+}} Butt Bombs effect on {{i|Dr. Fetus}} or {{i|Epic Fetus}} does not heal Brownie.
** {{dlc|r}} The skeleton version of {{c|Tainted Forgotten}} in the [[Hot Potato]] challenge <u>does</u> heal Brownie. Thus, butt bombs should be skipped to avoid a potential softlock.
* {{i|Flush!}} kills Brownie instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 {{e|Brownie Corn}}s.
* If Brownie is inflicted by any [[status effect]], he leaves a [[creep]] with that same effect (e.g. {{i|Spider Bite}} gives him [[white creep]] if he's affected).

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
Hush begins with a fight identical to the first phase of the {{E|???}} fight, having the same attacks and behavior but with a different appearance, half of ???'s health, and longer projectile travel distance due to being fought in a 2×2 room.

''See {{e|???}} for more details''.

=== Phase 2 ===
After Hush's first form is defeated, it reveals its large true form at the top of the room, taking the form of its splash screen portrait.
* During this phase, Hush occasionally sinks into the ground, becoming non-attacking and invulnerable, and only returning once most of the projectiles onscreen have dissipated. It performs this move every time it loses around 20% HP and also in conjunction with some of its later attacks.

==== Phase 2-1 (100-80% HP) ====
Hush remains stationary in the top center of the room and performs the following attacks:
* Fires barrages of yellow, blue, and green glowing projectiles in certain patterns, combining 1-3 different patterns of projectiles. These patterns include:
** Rings of projectiles that alternate between rotating clockwise and counterclockwise as they move outwards.
** U-shaped salvos aimed at Isaac.
** Lines of projectiles aimed at Isaac that either gain (yellow), lose (blue), or maintain (green) momentum as they travel (these lines have spaces between them every 4-5 shots).
** 2-4 repeating volleys of 4 projectiles, with equal spacing between each volley (the angle these volleys are shot out at rotates as the attack continues).
The same pattern can be used multiple times in each barrage, and projectile patterns become less dense if multiple patterns are used in the same barrage.

==== Phase 2-2 (80-60% HP) ====
Hush sinks into the ground and relocates to the center of the room before resuming its attacks. It also gains the following attack patterns, in addition to attacks from the previous phase:
* Hush's projectile barrage can include two new patterns:
** A very dense ring of projectiles, with a gap aimed somewhere towards Isaac's general direction.
** 3-5 spirals of projectiles, with even spacing between each spiral (projectiles from these spirals initially lose momentum, but after a few seconds they resume their normal speed while rotating counterclockwise as they move out).
* Spawns a cluster of {{e|Hush Fly|text=Hush Flies}} that either orbit Hush, launch towards Isaac's position and fly off-screen, or actively chase Isaac. These flies have invincibility for a short time after being spawned, and alternate between forming the shapes of a circle, triangle, square, pentagon, or a 5 or 6-pointed star.

==== Phase 2-3 (60-40% HP) ====
Hush keeps its attacks from previous phase and gains two more attacks and an extra shot pattern:
* Hush’s projectile barrage can now also include a very wide spread of projectiles that closes in on where Isaac was standing when fired.
* Hush spawns a horde of {{e|Blue Gaper}}s, before sinking into the ground to relocate. While relocating, Hush can summon {{e|Blue Boil}}s.
* Hush fires three rows of wavy {{i|Continuum}} projectiles in one of the cardinal directions, which warp over to the other side of the screen and increase in speed the longer they travel. Hush performs this attack 2-5 times before using a different one. These projectiles move in a set pattern and leave safe zones that last the entire barrage.

==== Phase 2-4 (40-20% HP) ====
Hush keeps its attacks from previous phases, gains an extra attack, and modifies its shot patterns:
* Hush sinks into the ground while firing its projectile barrages, moving in a random direction or chasing Isaac as it fires, and spawning Blue Boils as it moves. Only shot patterns from phase 2-1 can be used; the patterns added in phase 2-2 and 2-3 are lost.
* Hush creates three large red projectiles that move outward and split into 3 more projectiles multiple times. The split shots move quickly when they spawn but slow down before splitting again. Hush can start other attacks before the projectiles from this attack fully dissipate.
* {{Dlc|rnr+}} From this point onward, the cooldown between each of Hush's attacks is drastically reduced due to a bug.

==== Phase 2-5 (<20% HP) ====
Hush keeps most of its attacks from previous phases, but loses its ability to spawn Hush Flies. However, it gains one more attack in this phase:
* Hush fires two laser beams upward from its eyes, which creates beams on the ground that move toward Isaac and leave trails of slippery [[Creep#Blue Creep|Blue Creep]]. The speed at which the beams move is based on Isaac's speed stat, and are always possible to outmaneuver. While firing these lasers, Hush also releases five wavy, slow-moving lines of projectiles in all directions.
* {{Dlc|nrr+}} When at <1% health, there is a greatly reduced delay between Hush's attacks.
* {{Dlc|r}} If too much time passes without damaging Hush, it will regenerate some health. This removes the effectiveness of some very slow fight strategies (such as {{I|Gnawed Leaf}} combined with less effective familiars) that would have been successful (if slow) in previous versions.

sections.Strategies:
* Effects that cause long-lasting mass slowdown such as {{I|Stop Watch}} or the I'm Drowsy [[Pills|pill]] are very valuable, aiding the player's ability to dodge the complex tear patterns and deal with the massive spawns of enemies, which can happen in quick succession.
** The {{I|Broken Watch}} item can also cause a mass slow, but using it may not be a good idea since it also has a chance to speed up the entire room, making the fight extremely difficult.
** {{I|Night Light}} or {{I|Censer}} can apply tear slowdown on a smaller scale than the watch items, but their hard-to-control areas of effect may cause more confusion than benefit.
** {{Dlc|r}} The I'm Drowsy pill should '''not''' be used against Hush. The laser beams summoned in the final phase move at a speed based on Isaac's own base speed, but the slowdown from I'm Drowsy is not accounted for. Using it during the Hush fight will make it impossible to outrun the lasers.
* Any items that can block or deflect projectiles will be highly useful, due to the bullet-hell design of the fight. [[Orbital familiar]]s, {{i|Circle of Protection}}, {{i|The Soul}}, {{i|Trinity Shield}}, {{i|Dry Baby}}, {{i|Farting Baby}}, {{i|Host Hat}}, and {{i|Infamy}} may greatly help mitigate damage.
** Dry Baby's {{i|The Necronomicon}} effect will trigger very often due to the amount of projectiles, allowing to easily wipe out the large waves of enemies Hush can spawn.
** {{I|Psy Fly}} is especially helpful, as it both deflects a large number of projectiles, and only has a small cooldown after deflecting multiple.
** {{I|Saturnus}} may help with the large amount of bullets, but the tears in the ring at the start of the room may have fallen by the time Hush's shots reach you.
** {{I|Ocular Rift}} can trivialize most of Hush's attacks as projectiles are pulled towards the rifts and away from Isaac. However, rifts can also disrupt the projectile patterns, making dodging significantly more difficult.
* {{i|Lost Contact}} may be beneficial or detrimental depending on the player's tears stat; in combination with a high tears stat, many Lost Contact tears may still reach Hush even after blocking Hush's shots, but if the player has a low tears stat, they may find all their Lost Contact tears fired being destroyed during Hush's bullet hell attacks before they can reach their target.
** When the player has [[piercing tears]], however, Lost Contact can cause dodging most attacks to become trivial regardless of the player's tears stat, as the player's tears will destroy any enemy projectiles they come into contact with while remaining themselves intact.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Serpent's Kiss}}, {{i|Maw Of The Void}}, {{i|Athame}}, or {{i|The Virus}} (in combination with defensive items like {{p|Algiz}} or {{i|Book of Shadows}}) will make Hush's summoned enemies occasionally drop black hearts, allowing the player to farm large quantities of health during the enemy-spawning attacks.
** {{Dlc|r}} Serpent's Kiss only generates black hearts from contact damage. Maw Of The Void, Athame, and The Virus no longer generate black hearts at all.
* {{i|Broken Modem}} is not recommended, as it will stop Hush's tears and close some escape routes, making it harder to dodge in some cases.
** {{Dlc|r}} Tears affected by {{i|Broken Modem|n}} will be deleted rather than frozen in place, making the fight much easier.
* {{dlc|a+}} The combination of {{i|Mysterious Liquid}} and {{i|Trisagion|n}} can kill Hush extremely quickly by spawning massive amounts of creep under his large body.
* {{C|The Forgotten}}'s ability to swap characters into The Soul is very helpful in the Hush fight. Since nearly all of Hush's attacks are projectile-based, The Soul can hide behind the skeletal body and deal damage while staying totally safe.
* {{dlc|r}} Magnetizing Hush using {{I|Lodestone|n}} causes many of the slower bullets to not be able to go further than Hush's own hitbox, rendering the barrage ineffective.
* {{I|Cursed Eye}} can greatly benefit {{c|Keeper}}/{{c|Tainted Keeper}} if given the right items. They can fight Hush, and if they get damaged while charging, they teleport out of the fight and can go back to the shop area and bomb the {{e|Donation Machine}} to replenish health.
** {{T|Cursed Skull}} also works for this.
*** {{Dlc|r}}The {{e|Donation Machine}} can only be bombed once, after which it is destroyed for the rest of the run.
* Hush' {{e|Blue Gaper}}s spawning attack is useful for healing when playing as {{c|Tainted Magdalene}}.

* Releases 2 rings of 5 flames which expand outwards and rotate in opposite directions.
* Releases one large ring of 9 flames that expands outwards.

Bumbino slowly moves towards Isaac and can perform the following attacks:
* Swipes forward to clear a path to Isaac if Bumbino is obstructed by obstacles while chasing him.
* Performs two swipes, one in Isaac's direction, followed by another swipe in the opposite direction; these swipes can break obstacles. Then slams the ground, releasing 8 rock projectiles in all directions as well as 4 rock waves diagonally.
** If Bumbino hits a wall or a pit with a swipe he is momentarily stunned, interrupting this attack and causing rock projectiles to fall from the ceiling.
** His swipe attack will also deflect incoming projectiles.
* Charges in Isaac's direction when vertically aligned with him and a wall, breaking all obstacles caught in his path. Bumbino will become stunned upon impacting the wall, launching a cluster of rock projectiles in the opposite direction and causes rock projectiles to fall from the ceiling.

sections.Notes:
* If any member of the [[Seven Deadly Sins]] is defeated on the current floor, then Greed and {{e|Super Greed}} cannot spawn on that floor's shop.
** Therefore, exploring every room for a {{r|Mini-Boss Room}} and opening the {{r|Secret Room}} is the best way to minimize the odds of Greed appearing.

* Once Greed is encountered in a Shop or Secret Room, {{e|Super Greed}} replaces him in subsequent Shops and Secret Rooms. After Super Greed is encountered in the same manner, they cannot spawn in Shops or Secret Rooms for the rest of the run.
* Defeating Greed in a Secret Room causes all entrances to adjacent room entrances to be opened. {{dlc|nr+}} The exceptions are entrances to adjacent {{r|Challenge Room}}s and {{r|Boss Challenge Room}}s- which will be barred and blocked off forever, unable to be opened by a bomb.
* If Isaac teleports out of the room after defeating Greed but without killing all the Hoppers he spawns, Isaac can re-fight Greed for extra coins or copies of Steam Sale.
* {{dlc|nr}} Greed can drop {{i|Steam Sale}} even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. 
* {{dlc|a}} Greed spawned by blowing up a special shopkeeper can never spawn as Super Greed, even if another Greed was encountered before.
* {{dlc|r}} The exact spawn chances for Greed/Super Greed are as follows:
** Base chance 33.3%
** Having more than 20 coins entering the floor: +1.66%
** Destroyed the {{e|Donation Machine}} on the previous floor: +3.33%
** Destroyed a {{e|Shopkeeper}} in the previous floor: +0.66%
** Donated money to the {{e|Donation Machine}} in the previous floor: -1.66% per coin, up to a maximum of -8.33% for 5 coins
** These put the minimum and maximum chances at 25% and 39% respectively.

* If Big Horn tosses a bomb into one of the empty holes, Big Horn’s hand appears out of that hole and tosses out the same type of bomb.
* Quickly slaps the ground 3 times with an empty hand while traveling towards Isaac.

* {{dlc|r}} Holds up a Little Horn in his palm which spits out 3 small homing {{e|Dark Ball}}s in quick succession.

* Spits out a large Dark Ball beneath him that homes in on Isaac.
* Spits out two large Dark Balls beneath him that travel diagonally, bouncing when colliding with walls or Isaac's tears. These do not home.

=== Phase 1 ===
Clutch always spawns alongside 3 {{e|Clickety Clack}}s that it utilizes in its attacks. Phase 1 uses the following pattern:
* Randomly possesses one of the three Clickety Clacks, causing its head to spin and shoot 8 bone shots in the cardinal and ordinal directions. While possessing a Clickety Clack, Clutch is immune to all damage.
** Clutch will swap between Clickety Clacks at random intervals, or when the Clickety Clack he is possessing is killed. It can be briefly damaged when it is flying between Clickety Clacks.
** The possessed Clickety Clack will pursue Isaac and fire chains of bone projectiles at him when lined up in a cardinal direction, similar to a {{e|Bony}}, but will also move along a cardinal axis to stay in line with Isaac' position while shooting.
** The other non-possessed Clickety Clacks will be shielded, akin to the shield from a {{E|Bishop}}.
* When a Clickety Clack is killed, the bone pile it leaves behind will not regenerate. Instead, it will spawn a small purple fire that occasionally summons a bone projectile on its position before shooting it at Isaac, similarly to a {{e|Necro}}.
* When all three Clickety Clacks are killed, Clutch will be forcefully ejected and stunned, making it open to attack.
** After enough damage is dealt, Clutch will scream and revive all three Clickety Clacks, restarting the process.

=== Phase 2 ===
Phase 2 begins once Clutch reaches 25% health. Clutch will scream, destroy all of the Clickety Clacks, and spawn bone orbitals that orbit Clutch and block tears.
* The bone orbitals follow Clutch loosely, dragging behind its movements.
* Indestructible purple fires will be left in the wake of the dead Clickety Clacks.
In this phase, Clutch will only perform the following attack:
* Rushes to Isaac's position in the room, stops, and shoots six volleys of six purple flames, in an alternating pattern.
** Clutch repeats this attack until its health is depleted.
* Upon death, Clutch creates a large explosion that deals 4 ticks of 80 damage to all monsters.
sections.Notes:
* If  {{i|Eraser}} is used on Clickety Clacks prior to entering the boss room, the boss fight will begin directly in the second phase.
* If all the Clickety Clack bone piles are destroyed in Clutch's first phase through items such as {{i|Euthanasia}} or {{p|Chaos Card}}, it will automatically be forced into its second phase but without the purple fire places or bone orbitals.
* Clutch can be killed at 50% hp using {{i|Vade Retro}}.
* {{i|Vanishing Twin}} spawns a second Clutch in its second phase as there are not enough Clickety Clacks.
* {{I|Flush!}} will convert all Clickety Clacks into poop, immediately starting the second phase.
* Items like {{i|Uranus}} and {{i|Freezer Baby}} allow the Clickety Clacks to be frozen and destroyed, giving an easier time with the battle.
* The {{i|D10}} will downgrade the Clickety Clacks into Globins and start the second phase.
* Using {{i|Meat Cleaver}} isn't recommended until the second phase of the fight, as it will also split the invulnerable Clickety Clacks.

sections.Behavior:
Delirium's main form is stationary but teleports erratically around the room and performs the following attacks:
* Continuously sends out various overlapping patterns of white projectiles for the entire duration of the fight:
** 20 projectiles that slowly rotate clockwise or counterclockwise while expanding.
** 16 projectiles outwards in all directions.
** 14 projectiles that rotate clockwise, counterclockwise, or back and forth while expanding.
** 10 projectiles that fluctuate in and out while expanding.
** 8 slow-moving green-tinted {{i|Ipecac}} projectiles in all directions.
** 6 projectiles that travel outwards in a zig-zag pattern.
** 4 projectiles outwards in a lop-sided cross.
** 4 lines of 3 projectiles that spiral outwards.
** A spread of 5 projectiles in Isaac's direction.
** A burst of projectiles that travel outwards in random directions.
** A stray short-range projectile in a random direction.
*** The projectile size per each attack is random and varies from very small to moderately large.
* Transforms into bosses previously encountered during the run, which can include major bosses such as {{e|Mom}} or {{e|It Lives!}}.
** When it transforms into a boss, Delirium retains its own health, not the health of the boss it transformed into.
** When transforming into certain multi-phase bosses, such as Isaac, Delirium copies the phase that that boss would be at, given its current health percentage.
** When transforming into a segmented boss, only the first two segments share Delirium's hp; the other segments have separately generated hp and can be defeated separately.
** In rare occasions, it can transform into two or even three bosses at once.
** In rare occasions, it spawns a separate copy of the boss it transformed into.
** Whether it turns into a Champion variant or a regular variant is random and does not depend on which variant was previously defeated.
** {{dlc|nr}} It is unable to properly transform into Hush's true form. In order for this to happen, very few bosses must be encountered in the run. Additionally, many of Hush's attacks do not work properly and the sprite is also unfinished.
** {{dlc+|r}} Can transform into {{e|Baby Plum}}, {{e|Bumbino}}, and {{e|The Pile}}, but only Baby Plum has a unique sprite. Cannot transform into any other <u>Repentance</u> bosses.{{dlc-}}
** {{dlc|r}} Cannot transform into {{e|Mega Satan}}, rendering its unique sprite unused.
* Occasionally, it returns to its main form to perform projectile attacks at a faster pace.
* As it takes damage, it becomes more aggressive: moving, teleporting, transforming, and attacking at a faster rate.
** {{dlc|r+}} {{e|Mom|}} and {{e|Satan|}}'s second phase are exempt from the faster attack speed, instead attacking at a fixed speed.
** It also takes on a reddish hue to signify this change.
** Destroying non-Delirium segments when it transforms into segmented bosses can also temporarily trigger this effect.
** If Delirium is being dealt damage at a significantly high rate from multiple tear sources, it will attack, teleport, and transform at extreme speeds.

Upon defeat, the screen starts to glitch, fills with static, and the room switches between different environments, while short scenes from the current run are played ending with Delirium screaming and bursting into a small puddle of blood.

sections.Notes:
* Delirium is immune to {{p|Chaos Card}}.
* Upon defeating Delirium, Isaac gains 2 charges for his [[Active Collectible|active item]].
* {{i|Plan C}} can be used to kill Delirium. After Plan C is used against Delirium, when pausing in the instant of each flash from Delirium's death animation, the animation can be skipped before the death from Plan C's 3 seconds delay; this works because each flash from Delirium's death animation is still played when the game is paused.<ref>https://www.reddit.com/r/bindingofisaac/comments/nsc1pw/in_addition_to_my_other_post_how_to_kill_delirium/</ref> It is also recommended to position Isaac on the chest spawn location before Plan C's death occurs.
** It works with {{I|Lazarus' Rags}}, as it revives Isaac on the spot. However, the Completion Mark will go towards Lazarus, not the character originally selected.
** {{dlc+|r}} {{p|Soul of Lazarus}} and {{I|Inner Child}} revive Isaac in the same room he died in, and the Completion Mark goes toward the selected/current character.{{dlc-}}
** {{dlc+|r}} While playing as {{C|Tainted Lost}}, {{I|Birthright}} revives him inside Delirium's room without transforming himself into another character.{{dlc-}}
** {{dlc|r+}} This is no longer necessary, as {{i|Plan C}} will kill Isaac in 10 seconds after being used inside Delirium's room, which is enough time to let its death animation finish, and reward the completion mark for the current character before [[Isaac's Last Will]] pops up.
* Most entities that are considered to be bosses by the game (usually identified by ones that add the boss health bar to the screen, though there are exceptions) are marked as bosses that Delirium can transform into.
* Delirium's transformations have a huge amount of quirks and odd mechanics, and as such are practically impossible to fully document. A good amount of these quirks are documented below.
** Delirium can transform into either form of {{e|Satan}}.
** When transformed into the {{e|Gurglings}} or the {{e|Turdlings}}, it only appears as one instead of two.
** When transformed into {{e|Headless Horseman}}, it transforms into either the head or the body, but it doesn't transform into both at the same time.
** If Delirium transforms into {{e|Isaac}} and Delirium's health is low enough, it will attempt to perform Isaac's {{I|Crack the Sky}} attack. However, because Delirium's boss arena is a quadruple-sized room, the attack will cover half of the arena, making it extremely deadly.
** Each size of {{e|Fistula}} and {{e|Teratoma}} count as a separate boss, which Delirium can transform into just like any other boss.
** This also results in many bugs due to unaccounted for transformations. These can be viewed in the [[#Bugs|bugs]] section of this page.
** When transformed into two instances of the same boss (like {{e|Lokii}} or {{e|Sisters Vis}}), one of them can be killed but the other cannot (until Delirium's hp fully runs out).
*** If Delirium transforms into Pink Champion {{e|Monstro}}, it only takes the form of one and summons an extra Pink Champion Monstro.
**** This is also true for Pink Champion {{e|Polycephalus}} and Pink Champion {{e|The Cage}}.
*** If Delirium transforms into {{e|The Lamb}}'s second phase then undergoes another transformation, the body doesn't disappear and can be killed, just like the original Lamb's body.
**** Killing this body will cause the screen to become darker for a period of time, just like when you kill the original Lamb's body.
**** Delirium can also transform into the Lamb's body on its own. If this happens, the body disappears when Delirium transforms again.
** When transformed into a boss that has multiple segments, the extra segments can be killed. The head, however, cannot.
*** This also applies to {{e|Gemini}} — Suture can be killed but Contusion cannot.
**** If Delirium transforms into Gemini, then undergoes another transformation, Suture doesn't disappear. Instead, he continues to chase Isaac as if Contusion was killed in the original fight.
** Delirium's {{e|Mom}} form only stomps and does not spawn enemies.
* {{dlc+|r}} If a segmented worm-boss such as {{e|Larry Jr.}} or {{e|Scolex}} is removed via {{i|Eraser}}, Delirium will disappear if it attempts to turn into that boss. This will spawn the ending chest and count as having defeated Delirium. Other multipart bosses' erased pieces may be unable to spawn, but do not kill Delirium entirely.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|nr}} If Delirium transforms into Mega Satan, the boss maintains the ability to spawn the Harbingers, the Super Sins, and the Fallen Angels, and can do so in quick succession depending on Delirium's health. This can make the fight much longer, as attacking the bosses spawned by Delirium will have no effect on Delirium's actual health.
* Delirium can transform into Fallen {{e|Uriel}} and Fallen {{e|Gabriel}} but they don't have unique Delirium skins.
* Each time Delirium transforms, its [[Status Effects|Status Effect]] timer resets, allowing for useful effects to be active for a large portion of the fight if re-inflicted frequently enough.
** This quirk is especially useful in conjunction with the petrification from {{I|Mom's Contacts}}, as it can hold Delirium in place each time it is petrified, making it a much easier target to hit.
sections.Strategies:
* Just like with {{e|Hush}}, effects that cause long-lasting mass slowdown such as {{i|Stop Watch}} or the I'm Drowsy pill are very valuable, aiding the player's ability to dodge the complex tear patterns and deal with the massive spawns of enemies, which can happen in quick succession.
* {{dlc|r}} {{i|Broken Modem}} can also remove a lot of bullets, making it a must-have against Delirium.
* Delirium's main form lacks any damage scaling or armor, allowing the opportunity to deal high damage attacks against its massive base HP. Be wary that dealing significant bursts of damage against Delirium will also quickly increase its aggressiveness.
* One may wish to save this fight with {{c|Tainted Eden}} for the last mark of a file, as {{achievement|Corrupted Data|n}} can make {{r|I AM ERROR}} and {{r|Secret Room}}s worse.

sections.Behavior:
The Gurglings spawn as a pair and wander around the room. Each individual Gurgling has one attack in total which is performed independently of the other:
* Rushes towards the player when aligned in any cardinal direction, leaving behind damaging [[Creep#Red Creep|Red Creep]] until they have run into a wall.
** After rushing into a wall, they pause for a brief moment, and then spawn 0-2 {{e|Attack Fly|text=Attack Flies}}.
** Their dash can be interrupted if they run into an Attack Fly.

=== Phase 1 ===
* Spawns a {{e|Pooter}}.
* Jumps and shoots a radial of 8 tears in all directions on landing.
* Charges towards Isaac at high speeds, sliding while bouncing off obstacles and walls, She gradually loses speed before coming to a full stop.
** Any Pooters caught in her charge will be killed.
** The course of her charge can be affected by Tear knockback
** If Gurdy Jr. charges into an active bomb, she is slowed down tremendously.

=== Phase 2 ===
* When she has less than 50% health, she uses her charge attack continuously.
sections.Notes:
* Slowing Gurdy Jr. will, for the most part, render her charge attack useless.
* {{Dlc|nr}} [[Piercing tears]] lack knockback and cannot be used to divert or stop Gurdy Jr.'s charge attack.
* If Gurdy Jr. is [[fear]]ed/[[confusion|stunned]] during her charge attack after the effect wears off, she will immediately charge at Isaac.
* Gurdy Jr's charge attack has no telegraphing, making it very dangerous to stay close due to the lack of a warning.

sections.Behavior:
Dingle remains stationary and performs the following attacks:
* Fires 3 projectiles towards Isaac.
* Whistles before summoning 1-3 Dips and then fires 3 projectiles at Isaac.
* Quickly performs 3 long dashes towards Isaac while bouncing off obstacles and walls, after which he pauses to catch his breath.
** Dips caught in his dashes are knocked back a distance.
** Occasionally, Dingle will leave behind a {{g|Poop}} while using this attack.

Chub moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:
* Charges at Isaac whenever she lines up with one of her cardinal directions.
** Chub eats any {{e|Bomb}}s dropped in her path; stunning her for a moment before dealing considerable damage.
* Spawns 1-2 {{e|Charger}}s, up to a maximum of 5 (occasionally 6 if she spawns 2 while there are 4 alive).
** Chub's charge attack can damage and kill any Chargers.
Chub deals a whole heart of contact damage.
sections.Notes:
* Chub is often paired with Chargers in the boss room.
** {{dlc+|a}} She can also be paired with {{e|Drowned Charger}}s.{{dlc-}}
* When using {{i|Dr. Fetus}}' bomb combined with a shot type that passes through enemies, Chub will not eat the bomb.
* Each segment of Chub can be individually damaged, so a single piercing tear could hit Chub multiple times.
** {{Dlc|r}} Piercing shots no longer damage segmented enemies multiple times per attack.
* Chub will eat {{e|Troll Bomb}}s (such as those set by other bosses) just like bombs dropped by Isaac.
* {{i|Best Friend}} can damage Chub if eaten, similar to a bomb.
* {{i|Meat Cleaver}} can instantly kill Chub.
* Chub can spawn without the last segment.

sections.Behavior:
Gemini starts as a pair of bosses connected together by an umbilical cord.
* Contusion chases Isaac and periodically charges increasing his speed, but stops to catch his breath afterwards.
* Suture, while attached to Contusion, shoots a projectile towards Isaac if not behind an obstacle.
* If Contusion is killed first, Suture detaches and begins charging furiously at Isaac. He has high momentum and takes extra knock-back from tears, which can cause him to gain speed.
** If Suture is killed first, there is no change to Contusion's behavior.
sections.Notes:
* Status effects will equally affect both Contusion and Suture even if it was only applied to one of them. This includes effects granting knockback such as {{i|Knockout Drops}}.
** This also applies to Green Champion Gemini, despite the twins being completely separated entities.

Krampus.infobox:
{{infobox monster | id = 81 | variant = 1 | image = Boss Krampus {{dlc|nr|Old}} ingame.png | is mini-boss = yes | base hp = 60 | stage hp = 45 | environment = Mini-Boss
{{room|Devil}} | pool = {{i|A Lump of Coal}} (50% chance)
or
{{i|Head of Krampus}} (50% chance) | unlocked by = Krampus }} '''Krampus''' is a [[mini-boss]] that can occasionally appear inside of a {{r|Devil Room}}.

sections.Behavior:
Krampus moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:
* Stops and fires {{i|Brimstone}} lasers in all 4 cardinal {{dlc|a+}} or diagonal directions.
** {{dlc|a}} The lasers can sometimes rotate 90 degrees in either direction after being shot.
*** {{dlc|a+}} Krampus signals rotating {{i|Brimstone}} lasers by growling and quickly dashing towards Isaac before performing this attack.
* Fires 3 projectiles in a spread followed by 4 projectiles in a spread in succession towards Isaac.
Krampus deals a whole heart of contact damage.
sections.Notes:
* Encountering Krampus replaces both the statue of {{e|Satan}} as well as any deals in regular {{r|Devil Room}}s.
* Krampus can drop {{i|A Lump of Coal}} even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. However, he can only drop {{i|Head of Krampus}} once, and any other kills will only drop copies of {{i|A Lump of Coal}}.
* {{dlc|a}} Krampus can spawn in [[Greed Mode]] without needing to be unlocked.
** Defeating Krampus when encountered here still unlocks {{i|Head of Krampus}} even if Krampus himself has not yet been unlocked.
* {{i|Chaos}} will not change the items dropped from Krampus.
* {{dlc|r}} Krampus can never appear in the first {{r|Devil Room}} entered on a run.
sections.Unlockable Achievements: {{achievement text | Head of Krampus }}

sections.Behavior:
Great Gideon is always fought in a vertical double-size room and has no health in a traditional sense. Instead, Isaac must battle 6 waves of monsters to beat him, similar to [[Greed Mode]] waves. Each wave begins once all enemies from the previous wave have been defeated.

He uses the following attacks during these waves:
* Creates a vacuum that affects the whole room, pulling in Isaac and all monsters and monster projectiles. It also pulls in additional rock projectiles. Touching Gideon while he is performing this attack damages Isaac.
* Spits 5 projectiles in a cone shape towards Isaac. The center projectile is larger and splits into 8 projectiles in a radial burst when it lands or hits something.
* Charges up then spits large flame projectiles down the center of the arena that can occasionally leave small fires behind.
** Some enemies caught in this attack are turned into their flaming versions: {{e|Rock Spider}} into {{e|Coal Spider}}, {{e|Clotty}} into {{e|Grilled Clotty}} and {{e|Gyro}} into {{e|Grilled Gyro}}.
* After the beginning of the 4th wave, Great Gideon charges up and releases a rock wave down the center of the room, breaking parts of the floor and leaving gaps.
** There is always at least 1 gap between the trail of holes created by this attack as to not completely trap Isaac on either end of the room.
* Gideon does not spawn the next enemy wave during the middle of any of his attacks and only progresses a wave once he has finished.
After Isaac defeats all 6 waves of monsters, Great Gideon will deactivate, similar to a regular {{e|Stone Grimace}}.
sections.Notes:
* Great Gideon can be instantly killed with {{p|Chaos Card}}. Doing so reveals a unique 1x2 {{r|Crawl Space}} beneath him, containing two locked chests, two items and a random key.
** This can be done at any time, even if he has already been defeated, as his deactivated body still remains after returning to the room.
** Defeating Great Gideon in this way plays a unique animation in which the Chaos Card gets lodged in his forehead before he explodes.
** Pressing on a {{g|Kill Plate}} in the room similarly kills Great Gideon, and reveals the unique 1x2 {{r|Crawl Space}}. This also plays the unique animation of the {{p|Chaos Card}} in his head. Doing so is possible with {{i|D12}}
* Completing waves will not charge active items.
* {{i|Vanishing Twin}} will duplicate Great Gideon and increase the number of waves by 2. The waves themselves contain no extra enemies.
* Great Gideon can be fought outside the {{s|Mines}} or the {{s|Ashpit}} via using a {{p|IV - The Emperor?}} card in {{s|Downpour}} or {{s|Dross}}. If encountered outside his regular stages, he has preset waves consisting of {{e|Frowning Gaper}}s, {{e|Wall Creep}}s, {{e|Round Worm}}s, {{e|Gurgle}}s, and {{e|Sucker}}s.

Angel.infobox: The '''Angels''' are [[mini-boss]]es that can appear most commonly in {{R|Angel Room}}s. There are two angel variants: '''Uriel''' and '''Gabriel'''.

sections.Unlockable Achievements: {{achievement text | Dad's Key, The Family Man, Filigree Feather, Angelic Prism }}
sections.Notes:
* The angels will always alternate in order of appearance. Thus, if Uriel has just been defeated, the next angel spawn is guaranteed to be Gabriel and vice versa.
* If the player defeats an angel, and they already have both Key Pieces, no Key Piece drops. However, if this occurs, it counts as a normal room clear, and the player may be rewarded with a [[pickup]] or [[chest]].
* Angels only drop a Key Piece the first time they are defeated, even if Isaac does not pick up the Key Piece, subsequent kills in the same run provide no pedestal item rewards.
** {{dlc|a+}} Angels will drop a Key Piece even if they were defeated before. Additionally, if Isaac has one of the Key Pieces, angels will always drop the other piece, even if he already skipped that piece or that particular angel normally wouldn't drop it (for instance, Uriel will drop Key Piece 2 if Isaac already has Key Piece 1 from fighting him earlier).
* Rerolling {{i|Key Piece 1}} or {{i|Key Piece 2}} will yield an item from a pool, depending on which room the Key Pieces are in.
** Rerolling the Key Pieces in an Angel Room will yield an item from the Angel Room item pool.
* The angel's beams of light are rendered at a height, though their hitbox is on the ground (and their shadow is invisible). For diagonal beams, this causes Isaac to take damage even if he is below them, and allows him to partially walk into the beams if he is above them.
* {{dlc+|a+}} Angels will drop [[item]]s from the [[Angel Room (Item Pool)|Angel Room item pool]] instead of the Key Pieces if Isaac is holding {{t|Filigree Feather}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|a+}} Sometimes, two angel statues can appear in the same room. Destroying both at the same time will spawn both Uriel and Gabriel, but only one Key Piece will drop. If each angel is spawned and defeated separately, both will drop Key Pieces.
** {{dlc|r}} Both angels will drop key pieces if fought at the same time.
* Uriel and Gabriel are immune to the [[Fear]] effect.
* When spawned inside a {{R|Sacrifice Room}}, the room is not locked, allowing Isaac to simply walk out of the fight.
** When returning to the Sacrifice Room, the angel will be gone.
** {{dlc|na+}} As a result, it is possible to miss obtaining {{i|Key Piece 1}} while getting {{i|Key Piece 2}}.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
In its first phase, Dogma is attached to a television. Damage can only be dealt to Dogma by damaging the television in the center of the room. Any attacks towards Dogma itself causes a shield to briefly appear and block the attack. Dogma moves slowly towards Isaac, leaving a trail of damaging [[Creep#Static Creep|Static Creep]] and has a variety of attacks:
* Fires three consecutive radial bursts of 8 {{i|Godhead}} projectiles. If Isaac stands within the projectiles' auras for long enough, a {{i|Crack the Sky}} beam hits Isaac from above.
* Fires four consecutive bursts of projectiles in groups of 1, 2, 3, and 4 in each of the cardinal directions, with the overall pattern resembling a star.
** Occasionally after firing the 4th burst, Dogma greatly slows down all the projectiles mid-flight, leaving them to float around slowly for a moment before vanishing.
*** Dogma starts using this variant after losing around 60% of its HP, and performs it more frequently the lower its HP is.
* Fires 3 consecutive waves of 3 to 4 projectiles each in random directions. When these projectiles land, it creates thin, harmless rays that point towards Isaac and become damaging lasers after a few seconds.
* Fires a static {{i|Brimstone}} beam that bends towards Isaac. This beam is always fired in the closest cardinal direction to Isaac and switches if Isaac moves closer to a different cardinal direction.

=== Phase 2 ===
After destroying the television, Dogma falls apart into a puddle of static, before rising out of it as an orb and growing two pairs of wings resembling a [[wikipedia:Seraph|Seraph]]. During this phase, Dogma continues to chase Isaac between attacks, but becomes vulnerable and has completely different attacks:
* Fires a spread of disorganized feather projectiles towards Isaac if he's to its left or right.
* Summons a ball of light overhead which creates 16 to 18 harmless rays of light that point outwards and spin around the ball in random directions. After a few seconds, the rays stop moving and become damaging thin beams, similar to the ones used by the [[Angel]]s. This pattern is repeated three times, then Dogma throws it, firing one last wave of 8 wider beams in the cardinal and ordinal directions before dissipating.
** If the thrown ball of beams is slowed (by {{i|Stop Watch}} for instance), the 8 beams fire before being properly aligned.
* Turns into a winged wheel resembling an [[wikipedia:Ophanim|Ophanim]] and floats off-screen before charging back towards Isaac, continuing off-screen releasing a radial burst with three layers of feather projectiles with 12 feathers each near the end of the dash. It repeats this attack a total of 6 times.

As Dogma takes more and more damage during this phase, its Seraph form will occasionally flicker into various other forms; these include Isaac's head, a lamb's skull with a serpent in its eye, a fly, and a troll face with horns (each of which represents one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse). This is a purely visual effect.

When Dogma's HP reaches zero for the second time, it is destroyed as the whole screen fades to white before turning off like an old TV. Then Isaac is automatically given {{i|Dogma}} as the cutscene that introduces {{e|The Beast}} is played.
sections.Notes:
* After the beginning cutscene, Dogma appears very close to Isaac, making it easy to immediately take damage.
* Having a high speed is highly recommended for the second phase, as the charge attack can be almost unavoidable with low speed.
* {{i|Censer}} makes the second phase more difficult by reducing the space between feathers during Dogma's charging attack while not slowing Dogma itself. It is not recommended for this fight.
* If a {{i|Godhead}}-like projectile is "caught" with {{i|Telekinesis}}, it will be impossible to avoid the projectile's aura. As a result, taking damage is unavoidable.
* As the Dogma room is not counted as a Boss room, effects like {{i|Blanket}} will not occur in this fight.
* If Isaac has triggered the beginning cutscene, re-entering the room by any means (such as being revived outside the room as {{c|???}} with {{i|Ankh}}) will trigger the Dogma fight immediately.
* Before beginning the fight, going out and back into the living-room repeatedly while holding a trinket like {{T|Liberty Cap}} guarantees to get the best possible effect sooner or later, which can greatly help during the fight.
* {{i|Evil Charm}} will prevent Isaac from being affected by Dogma's {{i|Godhead}} aura projectile attack in its first phase.
* Any effect that lasts for one room won't remain after the fight and won't carry over to the [[Harbingers (Bosses)|Ultra Harbingers]] and The Beast fight.
* {{t|Perfection}} will spawn after defeating Dogma if the correct conditions are met, however, the trinket will be left behind when Isaac arrives to fight the Ultra Harbingers and The Beast.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
* Spawns four {{e|Death Scythe}}s along the walls of the room, aligned with Isaac in the cardinal directions. After a few seconds, they will accelerate towards Isaac.
** If Isaac is close to a wall, the scythe that would normally be spawned on that wall does not spawn.
* Spawns two Death Scythes in random positions around the room that constantly home in on Isaac until they are destroyed.
* Uses {{i|The Hourglass}} to slow Isaac down.

=== Phase 2 ===
After enough damage is dealt, Death will dismount from his horse. The horse has 150 HP, but it will also lose health when Death is damaged. Attacking the horse does not damage Death.
* Death occasionally spawns two {{e|Knight}}s and can have a maximum of two.
* Death's horse continuously flies horizontally across the room going off-screen and continuing on from the opposite end of the screen.
** Its charging patterns occur along 3 paths, starting with an upper charge into a middle charge a short distance below and finally a lower charge an identical distance below the middle path. It then restarts this process and can perform its upper charge in a new position in the room.
*** Its first charge will always leave room below it to allow for the lower second and third charges.
** The horse continues to charge even after Death has been defeated.
** It deals heavy damage to any enemy it runs into, except Death.
Both Death and his horse deal a whole heart of contact damage in both phases.
sections.Unlockable Achievements: {{achievement text | The Book of Revelations, 7 Seals }}
sections.Notes: * When Death uses The Hourglass, {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}'s tear is slow to respond and has a higher maximum speed, becoming difficult to control.

Lil Blub.infobox:
{{Infobox boss | dlc = r | files name = Lil Blub (Downpour) | id = 901 | variant = 0 | name = Lil Blub | environment = Boss

{{dlc|r+}} {{i|Aquarius}} (1% chance) }} '''Lil Blub''' is a [[boss]] added in ''[[The Binding of Isaac: Repentance]]'' that can appear in {{dlc|r}} {{s|Downpour}} and {{dlc|r}} {{s|Dross}}. __TOC__

sections.Behavior:
Lil Blub diagonally floats around the room and performs the following attacks:
* Spits up 2-3 {{e|Small Leech|text=Small Leeches}} that swarm around him, blocking shots.
* Spits out a single larger Small Leech that chases Isaac instead.
* Fires 6 streams of projectiles outwards in a radial burst. These projectiles deal a full heart of damage.
* Jumps once towards Isaac, creating a burst of disorganized arcing projectiles upon landing.
** Lil Blub can only use this attack when below a certain threshold of HP.
The previous two attacks also cause any Small Leeches that are swarming around Lil Blub to start chasing Isaac. Lil Blub cannot use any of these attacks if there are 6 or more Small Leeches in the room.
* Jumps towards Isaac 3-5 times, firing projectiles in the cardinal and diagonal directions upon landing. The cardinal shots are faster and travel further than the diagonal ones.
** Any leeches Lil Blub lands on are instantly killed.
** Lil Blub can only use this attack when below 25% HP, and greatly prefers using it if he can.

Upon death, he spawns 2-4 Small Leeches and bursts into a fountain of projectiles that rain down for a few seconds in a wide area.

Headless Horseman consists of two entities: The head and the body. Each performs attacks independently of the other.

The head has the following attacks:
* Shoots 3 projectiles in a spread at Isaac.
* Charges either left or right off-screen and reappears on the opposite end of the screen. He can charge either one, two or three times.
** He performs this attack more often if Isaac is to his left or right.
** This attack deals a full heart of damage.

The body has the following attack:
* Periodically shoots red {{i|Ipecac}}-like shots at Isaac, leaving a large puddle of damaging [[Creep#Red Creep|Red Creep]] on impact.
** This behavior is similar to {{e|Pestilence}}'s second phase.
Both the head and the body deal a whole heart of contact damage.
sections.Notes:
* In several normal rooms, Headless Horseman's head appears on his own without his body.
** Two or three of Headless Horseman's heads can be found in the same normal rooms.

sections.Behavior:
Clog remains stationary in the center of the room, with the exception of a rare boss room layout where he spawns at the top center. He performs the following attacks:
* Spits out a {{e|Drip}} below him, repeating this attack a random number of times.
** Clog stops spitting out Drips if 4 are already alive.
** Clog alternates between spitting out Drips and performing his other attacks. If 4 Drips are alive, he skips spawning them and continuously uses his other attacks.
* Creates three lines of farts that spread across the room, knocking away Isaac and Drips. Each fart has a chance to spawn {{g|Poop}}s.
** 1-2 {{g|Corny Poop}}s are spawned in this attack, and no more than 3 can be up at a time.
* Shoots out 4 spiraling lines of projectiles, consisting of either slow projectiles with small gaps in between or fast projectiles with large gaps in between.
** The projectiles pass over poop for 1 second after being fired, and are blocked by poop afterward.
** The gaps between the slower projectiles are barely large enough for Isaac to move between them if he is next to the left or right wall.
* Clog spins and causes the water in the room to circulate around him clockwise or counterclockwise, catching Isaac and any Drips, {{e|Bomb}}s, and/or [[Pickups]] in its current.
** This attack can only be used if at least 2 Drips are alive.
** Like other water-based effects in the {{s|Dross}} floor, Isaac is unaffected by this current if he has [[flight]].
* Upon Clog's defeat, he and all remaining Drips are "flushed" away identical to the effect of using {{i|Flush!}} on them.
sections.Notes:
* If a {{i|Butt Bombs}} Bomb goes off in the same room as Clog, it heals him.
* The hitbox of poops is small enough for Isaac and the Drips spawned by Clog to move diagonally between them, even if they are undamaged.
** This happens frequently when Clog causes the water to circulate and forces them to be pressed against the poops he spawns.
* All poops created by Clog are significantly less likely to spawn pickups until Clog is defeated and Isaac re-enters the room, at which point they return to having their normal pickup drop chance.
* {{i|Flush!}} kills Clog instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 {{e|Dip}}s.

sections.Behavior:
Blighted Ovum starts separated into two parts.
* Suture, now a ghost, is invincible and slowly floats towards Isaac, firing a horizontal {{i|Brimstone}} shot whenever Isaac is to his left or right. Suture cannot be killed and will die once Contusion does.
* Contusion constantly chases Isaac while leaving behind a trail of [[Red Creep]], and he periodically charges and gains speed. Unlike {{e|Gemini}}, he will not stop for a breath but slows down to his regular speed.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|a+nr}} Suture can be killed by {{i|Little Horn}}.{{dlc-}}
* If encountered in a Double Trouble boss fight, Suture's {{i|Brimstone}} laser can damage the other boss.

sections.Behavior:
Loki teleports to random locations in the room away from Isaac and has the following attacks:
* Shoots 4 projectiles in the four cardinal directions, followed by the four diagonal directions, and then the cardinal directions once again.
* Spawns a {{e|Boom Fly}} on top of himself. A maximum of 4 Boom Flies can be alive at once.
* Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions.
Loki deals a whole heart of contact damage.

A {{e|Poky}} can accompany Loki during the fight, dealing contact damage and blocking Isaac's tears.

{{dlc|r}} Loki can also be accompanied by 4 {{e|Stone Grimace}}s in the corners of the room.
sections.Notes: * Using the {{i|Meat Cleaver}} on Loki has a unique interaction, splitting him into {{e|Lokii}}.

sections.Behavior:
C.H.A.D. moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:
* C.H.A.D. charges at Isaac whenever he lines up with one of his cardinal directions.
** Like {{e|Chub}}, C.H.A.D. eats any {{e|Bomb}}s dropped in his path; stunning him for a moment before dealing considerable damage.
* Spawns 1-2 {{e|Sucker}}s.
* As he gets damaged, C.H.A.D. gradually shrinks in size and increases in speed and attack frequency.
sections.Unlockable Achievements: {{achievement text | Little C.H.A.D. }}
sections.Notes:
* {{Dlc|r}} C.H.A.D is much less common than his counterpart, spawning only 1/4th as often.
* C.H.A.D can spawn alongside 2 {{e|Boil}}s or 2 {{e|Red Boom Fly|text=Red Boom Flies}}.
* Each segment of C.H.A.D. can be individually damaged, so a single piercing tear could hit C.H.A.D. multiple times.
** {{Dlc|r}} Piercing shots no longer damage segmented enemies multiple times per attack.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
Hornfel appears with his own specially designed boss room: each wall has multiple boss doors with minecart tracks connecting each pair of doors. After a short delay, he appears out of a random door riding a minecart and performs one of the following attacks:
* Occasionally, when Hornfel enters the room through a door, he is accompanied by 2 {{e|Fly Bomb}}s.
* Throws 1-2 {{e|Bomb}}s at Isaac. Each bomb has a small chance of having the {{i|Hot Bombs}} or {{i|Sad Bombs}} effect.
* Throws 3 {{i|Brimstone Bombs}} that resemble mines. Each bomb has a delay and detonates after a few moments.
* Accelerates to a very high speed along one set of tracks, traveling in one direction, while frequently throwing out bombs. After multiple cycles, he slows down, gets sick, and vomits a fireball that releases fire trails in the cardinal directions upon landing.
* Sends out 1-2 decoy dummies with 4 HP on other tracks that burst into 6 {{e|Troll Bomb}}s if killed or walked into.
* Other minecarts occasionally appear on other tracks independent of Hornfel, carrying a {{e|Fire Place}}, {{g|TNT}}, or a variety of other enemies:
:: {{e|Bony}}
:: {{e|Faceless}}
:: {{e|Danny}}
:: {{e|Gurgle}}
:: {{e|Quakey}}

Hornfel and his decoys deal a whole heart of contact damage.

=== Phase 2 ===
Once Hornfel has taken enough damage, he falls out of his minecart and attempts to escape from the room via one of the doors surrounding the arena. He makes no attempt to attack Isaac, but he can still deal contact damage. In this phase, his contact damage is reduced to half a heart.

* Other minecarts carrying other monsters and objects can still appear as usual during this phase.
* If Hornfel escapes successfully, the fight ends as normal.
* If Hornfel is defeated, he unlocks {{i|Brimstone Bombs}} if not already unlocked, and has a 1/7 chance of dropping either {{i|Boom!}}, {{i|Brimstone Bombs}}, {{i|Hot Bombs}}, {{i|Remote Detonator}}, or {{i|Sad Bombs}} if it hasn't been seen or collected, otherwise he drops 3 {{e|Bomb}}s.
sections.Unlockable Achievements: {{achievement text | Brimstone Bombs }}

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
Chimera trots quickly in Isaac's direction, slowly building up speed. When fast enough, it leaves a trail of harmful [[green creep]] and makes wide turns due to its momentum. It can also perform the following attacks:
* Spits out 5 {{e|Small Maggot}}s.
** Any Small Maggots it walks into are killed.
** Unlike its other attacks, Chimera can perform this one without interrupting its chase and its built up speed.
* Spits out a {{e|Sick Boom Fly}} and throws it towards Isaac.
* Jumps twice towards Isaac, shooting out a radius of 8 tears on the first landing and 4 rock waves in diagonal directions on the second landing.

=== Phase 2 ===
Once its HP has dropped to about half, it makes a final charge towards Isaac before tripping and dividing the head and body into separate entities. It will take increasingly reduced damage as it approaches 50% HP until it transitions phases.
* The head continuously makes leaps towards Isaac and slides a distance after landing while leaving a trail of damaging [[red creep]]. It can also perform the following attacks:

After completing the final dash the body can pick the head up and throw it at Isaac, leaving a trail of projectiles as it travels and creating a burst of projectiles where the head collides with a wall.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
At the beginning of the fight, Mom's Heart is always accompanied by 2 {{e|Eye}}s. After a while, Mom's Heart retreats upwards, becoming invulnerable and launching four diagonal lines of red projectiles in a spread that slowly rotates clockwise. When each original Eye is killed, another one spawns in its place near the top of the arena.
* At any point during this sequence, if Mom's Heart's HP is brought below the threshold for her second phase, she will spawn {{e|Lump}}s instead of Eyes.

After the second set of Eyes have been killed, Mom's Heart alternates between two attacks:

* Lowers itself and shoots red projectiles in different patterns:
** 10 projectiles in all directions that expand outwards either continuously or in a pulsating manner.
** 2 streams of projectiles that spiral outwards.
** 2 rings of ten projectiles that pulsate outwards at different intervals.
** 8 slightly curved lines of projectiles that rotate and expand outwards slowly.

* After performing one of these projectile patterns for long enough, Mom's Heart retreats upwards again, shooting the same four slow-moving lines of projectiles, and spawns a number enemies of a singular type:
** 3 {{e|Flesh Mobile Host}}s
** 3 {{e|Globin}}s
** 2 {{e|Eye}}s
*** The type of monsters spawned in each wave is determined always follows the above order.
*** In the same manner as the original Eyes, a copy of each individual monster spawns again following the defeat of the original one.

* After all enemies have been defeated, Mom's Heart lowers itself and repeats the entire process.

=== Phase 2 ===
After reaching 60% HP, Mom's Heart beats slightly faster and continues the same behavior, but includes new projectile patterns and replaces the types of monsters it spawns.
* Its projectile patterns now include:
** A single line of projectiles that follows Isaac.
** 5 lines of projectiles that mimic Isaac's movements (these lines have no space between projectiles).
** 3 pulsating curved lines of projectiles that rotate and expand outwards. This pattern can occasionally change direction of rotation.

* Its spawned monsters are now:
** 3 {{e|Lump}}s
** 2 {{e|Swinger}}s
** 3 {{e|Globin}}s

=== Phase 3 ===
After reaching 30% HP, Mom's Heart beats much faster and no longer retreats upwards and instead performs projectile attacks and spawns enemies simultaneously. However, after finishing each projectile pattern, if there are any monsters alive, it will not perform another pattern until they are killed. In addition, a second wave of monsters no longer spawns after the first is killed.
* It gains one new projectile pattern:
** 4 curved lines of projectiles that continuously rotate and expand outwards.
* It loses the projectile patterns from the first phase except for the following 2:
** 2 streams of projectiles that spiral outwards.
** 8 slightly curved lines of projectiles that rotate and expand outwards slowly.

* Its spawned monsters are now:
** 4 {{e|Walking Boil}}s
** 4 {{e|Tumor}}s
** 4 [[Mask + Heart|Heart]]s

=== Phase 4 ===
After reaching 20% HP, Mom's Heart stops its previous attacks and shoots four diagonal {{i|Brimstone}} lasers that rotate either clockwise or counter-clockwise for a duration before stopping for a moment and then repeating the attack.
* The direction the lasers rotate depends on which is closest to Isaac when they are fired. The closer laser will rotate after Isaac and the rest will follow.
* The duration the beams rotate can be: 1 rotation, 1 and a half rotations, or 2 whole rotations.
* Upon defeat, Mom's Heart fires out a ring of 14 projectiles.

All of Mom's Heart's projectiles deal a whole heart of damage. The heart itself does not deal contact damage.

As most of Mom's Heart's projectile attacks are synced with the rhythm of the heart's beating, as the fight progresses, the speed of each projectile attack increases.

All of Mom's Heart's projectile attacks can hurt and kill spawned monsters.

'''Phase 1:'''
The battle begins with three {{e|Lil' Haunt}}s circling The Haunt, who floats around the room and is invulnerable. The Haunt and its Lil' Haunts can still do contact damage to Isaac while incorporeal.

{{infobox boss | id = 951 | dlc = r | variant = 0 | environment = Boss
{{floor|Home}} | appearance = The Beast | base hp = 10000 | portrait = no | pool = ''None'' }} '''The Beast''' is a [[boss]] added in ''[[The Binding of Isaac: Repentance]]'' DLC. She appears in {{s|Home}} and is the final boss of [[Endings#Ending 22 (Dogma)|Ending 22]], as well as ''The Binding of Isaac'' as a whole.

sections.Behavior:
After defeating {{e|Dogma}}, Isaac is given {{i|Dogma}}, granting him [[flight]] and allowing him to traverse The Beast's 2D [[Crawl Space]]-like arena. {{i|Dogma}} also grants a one-time {{i|Holy Mantle}} shield, the effect of {{i|The Wafer}} (if playing in Normal Mode), prevents Isaac's [[speed]] from going under 1.1, and +2 [[damage]], and heals him up to 6 [[Health|hearts]] with {{e|Red Heart}} Containers and {{e|Soul Heart}}s.

At the start of the fight, The Beast sits inactive in the background. Flying around The Beast are four [[Harbingers (Bosses)#Ultra Harbingers|Ultra Harbingers]], which attack Isaac one at a time in the order of {{e|Ultra Famine}}, {{e|Ultra Pestilence}}, {{e|Ultra War}}, and {{e|Ultra Death}}. Once they have all been defeated, The Beast lets out a roar, submerges into the lava, then reemerges on the right side of the screen, beginning her fight.

=== {{dlc|nr+}} Phase 1 ===
During her first phase, The Beast uses the following sequence of attacks, repeating indefinitely:
* Charges towards Isaac, forcing the screen to scroll while harmful, destructible stalagmites and stalactites move towards Isaac.
** The screen scrolls along with The Beast, meaning that she will not get closer to Isaac even if he doesn't move; this attack only brings the stalagmites and stalactites on-screen.
* At the end of the charge, The Beast begins to inhale large rings of fire which have one small gap that Isaac can fit through.
** Any remaining stalagmites or stalactites on-screen are destroyed at the start of this attack.
* After inhaling 8 rings of fire, The Beast stops and fires a colossal {{i|Brimstone}}-like beam that covers the bottom and middle portions of the screen.
* After this attack, she performs a quick charge across the screen before repeating the initial charge in the opposite direction. Similar to the {{i|Brimstone}}-like beam directly before, she covers a large portion of the bottom and middle parts of the screen.
Even if The Beast's HP drops below the threshold for her second phase, this will always still be the first attack she performs every single time.

=== {{dlc|nr+}} Phase 2 ===
The Beast enters her second phase below 6660 HP and loses her inhaling attack, but gains 2 new ones. Additionally, during the charging attack, there are more rocky obstacles and some stalactites are cracked and fall when Isaac passes underneath. (As before, the screen scrolls while The Beast charges, with Isaac's position on the screen being maintained.)

At the end of a charge, The Beast performs one of two attacks:

* Opens her mouth and fires 3 radial waves of slow-moving fire, then fires 6 radial strings of fast-moving projectiles which travel through the gaps left between each fire.
* Roars and spawns 4 Beast Souls which chase Isaac and charge at him, trying to predict his movements, before dissipating.
** Any remaining stalagmites or stalactites on-screen are destroyed at the start of this attack.

After using either of these attacks, The Beast submerges into the lava and causes glowing orange lines to appear beneath Isaac and in other random areas. The glow of these lines increases in intensity over time before launching out a large fiery projectile that flies up and falls back into the lava. The Beast gradually increases the rate at which projectiles are launched before eventually reemerging from the lava on the opposite end of the screen and launching a small burst of large fiery projectiles arcing in all directions.
* Any remaining stalagmites or stalactites on-screen are destroyed at the start of this attack.

=== {{dlc|r+}} Phases 1&2 ===
In [[The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+]], previous attacks from phase 1 and 2 are mixed together and not tied to HP. Phase 3 is still triggering at 33% HP.

=== Phase 3 ===
The Beast enters her third phase at 33% HP and is indicated by a burst of blood. The Beast is forced to submerge into the lava and reappear on the other side of the screen, then begins charging towards Isaac indefinitely while more stalagmites and stalactites spawn behind him. (As before, the screen scrolls while The Beast charges, with Isaac's position on the screen being maintained.) Cracked stalactites do not appear during this phase.

Once The Beast's HP reaches 2000, her horns crack and her body ruptures in boils. She degrades through two more stages: losing 2 horns and an eye upon reaching 1000 HP, and losing another eye, another horn, all of her teeth, and generally having a melted look upon reaching 500 HP. Upon defeat, a large light ray comes from above and strikes her down, followed immediately by [[Endings#Ending 22 (Dogma)|Ending 22]].

sections.Notes:
* Phase 2's narrow activation period (from 50% to 33% health) means it will often be skipped, typically if enough damage is done during the long-duration fire rings attack.
* {{i|Censer}} / {{I|Night Light}} is not recommended for this boss battle, as it can cause flames to pile up unavoidably during the Beast's fire ring inhalation attack.
* {{p|Chaos Card}} doesn't work on The Beast.
** If the fight is entered with a {{p|Chaos Card}} it will be converted to a [[Pills|Full Health]] pill
* {{p|Era Walk}}, "[[Pills|I'm Drowsy...]]" pill, etc. works for the duration of the fight, and makes for an easy battle.
* {{I|Sprinkler}} will float in the air for the duration of the flight and remains in place during the chase sequence, providing constant extra damage.
* {{i|Plan C}} works and will kill The Beast before dying, triggering [[Endings|Ending 22]]. It must be used after all four Ultra Harbingers are defeated, or else it will only kill the current Ultra Harbinger.
** However, if the "[[Pill|I'm Drowsy...]]" pill was used in the boss room, using {{i|Plan C}} would kill Isaac right before the Beast's death animation's end.
* All teleportation items/cards cannot be used to escape the fight; instead, Isaac will be teleported to a random spot on the screen. Similarly, any respawn items will respawn Isaac immediately, without restarting the fight. Essentially, there is no way to leave the fight after it has begun, outside of {{i|R Key}} and {{i|Forget Me Now}}.
** {{dlc|nr+}} {{i|Lil Portal}} is capable of creating a portal in the fight if it consumes enough pickups. Going into the portal will return Isaac to an unexplored room in {{s|Home}} and softlock the run as it is not possible to return to the boss fight.
* {{i|Ipecac}} and {{i|Haemolacria}} travel in an arc, similar to Ultra Pestilence's shots, and are extremely hard to aim. If Isaac has high [[range]] when firing left or right, the projectiles will go up and off-screen.
* Most non-flying [[familiar]]s, such as Super Meat Boy, {{i|Leech}}, or [[Familiars#Blue Spiders|Blue Spiders]], are almost completely useless against the Ultra Harbingers, as the familiars will stay stuck in the lava on the bottom of the arena. However, they can damage Ultra War if his movement pattern takes him close enough to the bottom of the screen, and The Beast as she is half-submerged in lava.
* Any item that gives an effect for the room, such as {{i|Box of Friends}} or {{i|The Book of Belial}}, will work for the entire fight, starting with Ultra Famine.
* {{i|Broken Watch}} can affect this fight. However, it only activates for 1 unvisited room out of 4. Finishing the fight with Dogma and beginning the fight against the Ultra Harbingers counts as a new visited room. Hence, to have the effect against The Beast, the last visited room in Home must be the 3rd after the effect was triggered for the last time.
* {{i|Gnawed Leaf}} works as normal in this fight — as long as Isaac stays still and has some way of dealing damage without moving or firing, such as an enemy-chasing familiar. He will eventually kill The Beast with enough patience.
* {{i|Flat Stone}} makes tears travel straight down, as there is no ground they can skip on.
* Like {{i|Flat Stone}}, bombs fired with {{I|Dr. Fetus}} will be fired in a downward arch since there's no ground for them to slide on, making it a difficult item to use in the fight without bomb immunity items such as {{i|Pyromaniac}} or {{i|Host Hat}}.
* Defeating each Ultra Harbinger will grant Isaac's active item 2 charges, similar to {{r|Boss Rush}}.
* {{c|The Soul}} is capable of dragging {{c|The Forgotten}} with him as he moves. This means he can move anywhere on the screen, but at a much slower rate. {{c|Tainted Forgotten}} flies during this battle and stays where he ends up when thrown (in mid-air), meaning that if you throw him at the Beast you can constantly attack its during the chase scenes.
* The hitboxes of stalactites, stalagmites, and the lava persist during The Beast's death animation.
* Despite not being able to fly or go over gaps in its final form, {{i|Bumbo}} will be able to "fly" around the arena and deal damage without sinking in the lava. Bombs placed by Bumbo still behave normally and fall.
* Bombs are affected by gravity and are hard to hit the Ultra Harbingers with, but can easily be used against The Beast, especially during chase sequences. As such, it is a great strategy to continuously use all of your bombs during this sequence, as there is no longer any other need for them. This also makes {{i|Curse of the Tower}} and {{i|Anarchist Cookbook}} safe to use as long as Isaac does not move too close to the bottom of the screen.
* Because there are no walls or floors for tears to collide with in this fight, the damage boost from {{i|Dead Eye}} will not fade away.
* Items that place [[Poops]], such as {{i|The Poop}} or {{i|Hallowed Ground}}, cannot place poops during the fight.
** However, poops will spawn if enemies are turned into poops (e. g. by {{i|E. Coli}}).
* The lava projectiles from both the lava and when The Beast rises afterward can be slowed and knocked down with certain slowing items such as {{i|Censer}} and high [[knockback]] tears.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
Min-Min floats slowly towards Isaac and performs the following attacks:
* Spits a {{e|Willo}} at Isaac which fires a projectile at him before returning to orbit around Min-Min. Min-Min can have a maximum of 4 orbiting her. Willos do not deal contact damage.
** This can be done multiple times in quick succession until the limit of 4 Willos has been reached.
** Willos orbiting Min-Min occasionally fire a projectile towards Isaac.
* Once Min-Min has 4 orbiting Willos, she periodically causes them to fire 3 projectiles outwards. If any Willos are killed during this attack the remaining ones perform this attack uninterrupted.

=== Phase 2 ===
In this phase, Min-Min burns away the husk surrounding her, and can now have a maximum of 7 Willos orbiting her. She will continue to float slowly towards Isaac and has new attacks:
* Min-Min spawns up to 4 Willos around herself and then causes all orbiting Willos to fire 3 projectiles outwards.
** Willos orbiting Min-Min still occasionally fire a projectile towards Isaac.
* Spits a Willo at Isaac which fires a projectile at him before returning to orbit around Min-Min.
* Causes the current orbiting Willos to fire 3 projectiles outwards.
* Sends her orbiting ring of Willos to chase Isaac. After a few seconds, they return.
* Disappears and creates several groups of lights on the ground. One group at a time, Willos appear from the lights, fire at Isaac, and disappear.

Upon Min-Min's defeat, all spawned Willos die alongside her.

The number of individual The Hollow bodies that can spawn each fight can vary from 1-4. The most common encounter with The Hollow is with 2 bodies.
* Flies around the room diagonally, bouncing off of walls.
** The Hollow appears to travel faster when moving at vertical angles compared to horizontal.
** The Hollow can change direction if it collides with Isaac.
