sections.Behavior:
Passing through the Golden Gate and stepping onto the pentagram initiates the Mega Satan fight.

=== Phase 1 ===
Mega Satan is accompanied by two hands, which serve as a barrier to protect him and an avenue for him to attack. His hands spread apart if Isaac gets close to him, and move together if Isaac moves away from him. Each hand has 600 HP, and destroying a hand deals 100 damage to Mega Satan. Each hand respawns 30 seconds after it’s destroyed.

Mega Satan has the following attacks:
* Closes his eyes and then fires one of several projectile patterns, including:
** 3-5 lines of blood projectiles. The angle these shots are fired at alternates between rotating clockwise and counterclockwise. The less lines of projectiles there are, the faster they travel and rotate.
** Spreads of brown projectiles that split into 4 smaller projectiles after traveling far enough, similarly to {{i|Cricket's Body}}.
** 2 spirals of blood projectiles that very rapidly rotate clockwise, creating semi-circular waves of projectiles.
** Rings of blood projectiles, fired in rapid bursts of 3.
** 2 spirals of blood projectiles that rotate clockwise at different speeds.
** 3 lines of blood projectiles that alternate between slowly curving right and left with every shot fired. The angle these lines of projectiles are fired out at alternates between slightly rotating clockwise and counterclockwise.
* Closes his eyes and then fires a {{i|Mega Blast}} laser straight down. His hands always fully spread apart while charging the laser, regardless of Isaac's position.
** The growl that telegraphs this attack is louder than usual, distinguishing it from his other attacks.
* Slams his head into the platforms 1-3 times, creating chaotic bursts of projectiles in all directions.
* Holds up one hand, then slams it at Isaac, creating a circular rock wave on impact. This attack can’t be used if both hands are currently destroyed.
* Slams both hands 3 times, alternating back and forth, creating rock waves that move towards the bottom of the screen. This attack can’t be used if either hand is currently destroyed.
** Destroying a hand during this attack prevents it from creating more rock waves.
* Mega Satan also spawns sets of [[All Mini-Bosses (Bosses)|mini-bosses]] to attack Isaac alongside him. These sets can be:
** {{e|Gluttony}} and {{e|Envy}}
** {{e|Sloth}} and {{e|Pride}}
** {{e|Wrath}} and {{e|Greed}}
** {{e|Lust}}
** {{e|The Hollow}}
*** These mini-bosses can be damaged by Mega Satan’s attacks. His laser deals 36 damage per tick, while all others deal 10 damage per hit.
* After taking enough damage, Mega Satan and his hands withdraw into the darkness behind him and become invulnerable. During this time, he spawns a wave of bosses or mini-bosses, which must be killed in order to make Mega Satan vulnerable again. The first waves of bosses begins after Mega Satan takes 750 damage, the second after 1,500 damage, and the third after 2,250 damage. He will withdraw but not spawn these waves if there are any remaining previously spawned bosses left. Only when the room is cleared does he spawn the following:
** Wave 1.1: {{e|Famine}} and {{e|Pestilence}}
** Wave 1.2: {{e|War}} and {{e|Death}}
*** There is a chance for all Horsemen to appear as their champion forms.
** Wave 2.1: {{e|Super Envy}}
** Wave 2.2: {{e|Super Lust}} and {{e|Super Wrath}}
** Wave 2.3: {{e|Super Sloth}}, {{e|Super Gluttony}}, {{e|Super Pride}}, and {{e|Super Greed}}
** Wave 3.1: [[Angel#Uriel|Fallen Uriel]]
** Wave 3.2: [[Angel#Gabriel|Fallen Gabriel]]

=== Phase 2 ===
After taking 3,000 damage, Mega Satan sinks into the darkness and rises in his final phase as a skull. He no longer has his hands, nor does he spawn bosses; instead, he fires complex projectile patterns. Possible patterns include the ones from the first phase (with increased shot speed), plus:
* 2 spirals of projectiles that slowly rotate counterclockwise. The shots zig-zag as they travel outward.
* 2 lines of projectiles that alternate between curving left and right. These lines combine to create curving lines with a safe space that moves from the left of the arena to the right.
* Rings of projectiles, with every other wave fluctuating in speed as it travels.
* Many lines of projectiles that slowly curve to the left (if black) and right (if red); these lines create safe spaces to maneuver in that slowly shift to the right.
* Several lines of projectiles that slowly wiggle as they travel, similarly to {{t|Wiggle Worm}}. The angle these shots are fired at either rotates clockwise or alternates between rotating clockwise and counterclockwise.
* Many lines of projectiles that wiggle as they travel and slowly curve to the left (if black) and right (if red); these lines create unmoving safe spaces between them.
* Many lines of projectiles that spin as they travel, similarly to {{t|Ring Worm}}. The angle these shots are fired at constantly randomizes.
** These projectiles don’t travel far enough to reach the corners of the arena if Mega Satan isn’t close to that corner.
* Dense rings of projectiles that wiggle as they travel.
* Several lines of projectiles that make large zig-zags as they travel.
* Six lines of projectiles, half of which slowly curve to the left (if black) and right (if red). These lines create safe spaces that slowly move towards Mega Satan.
* Rings of projectiles that rotate clockwise (if red) and counterclockwise (if black) simultaneously.
* Several lines of projectiles that continuously converge onto each other.
** The projectiles used in these patterns can be colored black, red, brown, or silver, depending on which one is used. For some attacks, they instead appear as red or yellow fire.

As Mega Satan takes damage during this phase, his skull begins to crack before eventually shattering. After this final phase is defeated, the game ends and [[Endings#Ending 16|Ending 16]] plays.

* {{dlc+|a+}} If {{s|The Void}} is unlocked, there is a {{dlcalt|50%|r+=100%}} chance that the game does not immediately end, and Mega Satan instead drops an ending chest along with a portal. Entering the chest ends the game and plays the cutscene, while entering the portal takes Isaac to {{s|The Void}}.{{dlc-}}

sections.Behavior:
The battle against Satan has three distinct phases.

=== Phase 1 ===
The first phase starts with a slight delay after Isaac enters the room:
* Satan shouts, and roughly two seconds after Satan's voice dies out, {{e|The Fallen}} spawns at the center, with two {{e|Kamikaze Leech|text=Kamikaze Leeches}} to either side.

=== Phase 2 ===
Once The Fallen is dead, the Devil Room statue at the top of the screen transforms into Satan's first form. He stays near the top of the room moving horizontally and performs the following attacks:
* Spits out 2 consecutive spreads of 5 and 4 projectiles towards Isaac. He chains this attack at least twice.
* If Isaac is to either side of him, he can:
** Shoot half-rings of 8 projectiles from both his hands towards the left and right sides of the room.
* If Isaac is below him, he can:
** Shoot two {{i|Brimstone}} lasers from his hands, that curve towards each other while leaving a gap in the middle.
** Charge up and fires a {{i|Brimstone}} beam from his mouth directly downwards.

If Satan is pushed too far away from the top center of the room, he will rapidly spring back to that position.

=== Phase 3 ===
After depleting his entire second phase health bar and reaching half of his total HP, he flies off-screen and has one attack:
* Stomps the ground with both of his feet at Isaac's previous positions, similar to {{e|Mom}}'s stomp attack, but with less delay. The stomps come down one after another, and after two stomps, they persist for a moment before both are retracted.
* Up to two Kamikaze Leeches continuously spawn during this phase.
** They can be killed by Satan's stomp, but will also deal considerable damage to him.
** There appears to be a maximum amount of Kamikaze Leeches that can be spawned, as they stop appearing if the fight draws out for too long and the Kamikaze Leeches are not killed.

Satan's projectiles and contact damage deal a whole heart of damage.

Once Satan is defeated, remaining Kamikaze Leeches die alongside him.

Upon entering this area, all [[Items#Passive Collectibles|passive items]], [[Items#Active Collectibles|active items]], and [[trinket]]s will be rendered inactive, and Isaac's {{e|Bomb}}s, {{e|Penny|text=coins}}, and {{e|Key}}s will be set to zero, leaving him similar to his state during the start of the game. He only has his current hearts. He must walk through several empty rooms before reaching the end room containing {{i|Knife Piece 2}}. Picking it up causes the room to shake and summons Mother's Shadow. Mother's Shadow is completely invulnerable and Isaac must escape her by returning to the special area entrance and leaving. On the way back, the path back will be obstructed by various obstacles, such as [[rocks]], {{e|Fire Place}}s, [[spikes]], and {{g|Poop}}s.

'''Mother's Shadow''', after appearing, begins slowly floating after Isaac. When close enough to him, she stops and then quickly dashes at Isaac, dealing a whole heart of contact damage. Isaac can 'push' Mother's shadow before her charge by walking into her and will not take contact damage. Mother's Shadow can go off-screen with her dash attack or when a door is crossed into a different room. She then resumes following Isaac.
* Mother's Shadow's position at all times is determined by her position relative to the general layout of the floor, meaning she persists in the same location even when Isaac moves through rooms. However, she cannot be left  behind and is carried along as the screen moves.
* After encountering Mother's Shadow, the previously empty path back to the main floor map becomes filled with a variety of [[obstacles]], such as poops that must be destroyed, timed spikes, rocks that must be broken by {{e|Throwable Bomb}}s from {{e|Bomb Grimace}}s, buttons, and sometimes keys and certain cards that spawn in each room.

As soon as Isaac passes the door leading out of the sub-area, Mother's Shadow screams Isaac's name in defeat and disappears as the sub-area's entrance is blocked by falling rocks. It is no longer possible to access this area again past this point.
sections.Notes:
* Upon acquiring the Knife Piece 2, all [[Fire Places]] are extinguished and then re-ignited as red fires as Mother's Shadow appears.
** Fire places can drop their pickups during this scene.
* After Mother's Shadow spawns and the Knife Piece room reopens, Isaac gains 1 charge for his [[Active Collectible|active item]].
* New [[pickups]] obtained in the area will persist after Isaac leaves.
* Unlike non-story items, which disappear during the sequence, Isaac's health stays the same, and [[Status Effects#Friendly|friendly]] enemies still follow him here.
** [[Blue Fly|Blue Flies]], [[Blue Spider]]s, [[Locust]]s, {{I|Big Fan}} spawned from a Pretty Fly Horse [[Pills|Pill]], {{I|Cube of Meat}} spawned from a {{I|Potato Peeler}}, and Wisps spawned from {{i|Book of Virtues}} and {{i|Vengeful Spirit}} persist into this sequence, but have no effect on Mother's Shadow. Blood clots spawned by {{i|Sumptorium}} will also persist and are immune to Mother's Shadow.
* Extra lives granted by items such as {{i|Dead Cat}} or {{i|Guppy's Collar}} do not work, as they are removed from Isaac.
** {{c|Lazarus}}, however, still retains his extra life.
* Items that grant [[flight]] are taken away, forcing most characters to traverse the obstacles normally.
** {{p|XIX - The Sun?}} allows any character to fly, despite not having the visual effects of the card's {{i|Spirit of the Night}} visible.
** {{p|XV - The Devil?}} also allows any character to fly. However, the effect is likely to wear off before the end of the chase sequence.
** {{I|Esau Jr.}} works similarly. If Isaac enters the zone with Esau Jr., he is still able to fly without his appearance.
* The active piece of {{i|Broken Shovel 1}} will still spawn Mom's feet in this area.
* {{c|Eve}} will benefit from her {{i|Whore of Babylon}} if criteria are met but her sprite will remain un-cursed.
sections.Strategies:
* The key to avoiding damage during the chase sequence is to be patient. Trying to rush to the exit door will often result in unavoidable hits.
* Mother's Shadow will not attack Isaac directly between dashes, only float in his general direction. She will scream right before attacking, and will lock her direction; stay in place until she starts to dash and then swiftly move out of the way to dodge.
* Going back into the previous room doesn't cancel her attacks, but provides more space for avoiding them, as well as invincibility frames.
* Do not stand on one tile-wide paths for too long, because they limit Isaac's ability to move out of the way of her dashes.
* Since Isaac keeps any health he enters the area with, it is wise to stock up on hearts beforehand to minimize chances of death.
** {{c|Tainted Eve}}'s {{i|Sumptorium}} should be used before entering to maximize health.
* {{C|Azazel}}, {{C|The Lost}}, {{C|Tainted Lost}}, {{c|Tainted Jacob}} in his Lost form, and {{C|Tainted Forgotten}} can escape with minimal risk, as they can use their inherent flight to fly directly to the exit door.

=== Phase 1 ===
The Frail in its first phase has 100 HP like {{e|Pin}} and behaves identically, with the only difference that The Frail is less accurate in its jumps and generally overshoots or undershoots Isaac.

=== Phase 2 ===
Upon its HP being depleted, The Frail's appearance becomes skeletal. It now has 200 HP and performs the following attacks:
* Jumps out of the ground towards Isaac, firing 4 diagonal projectiles from the last section of its body that each split into 4 more projectiles in either cardinal or diagonal directions.
** {{dlc|r}} Whether it fires projectiles depends on the length of its jump: does not fire projectiles on short jumps, fires projectiles shortly upon exiting the jump on regular/medium jumps, and fires projectiles both shortly upon exiting and after a few moments airborne on long jumps.
* Partially emerges head-first and:
** Fires a {{i|Brimstone}} laser at Isaac, rotating to follow his movements.
** Fires a quick, non-moving {{i|Brimstone}} laser at Isaac 2 times before stopping.
** After performing any of these attacks, The Frail will always jump out of the same spot it entered.
* Partially emerges tail-first and fires a burst of white projectiles in all directions which leave small puddles of slowing [[Creep#White Creep|White Creep]] where they land.
** After performing this attack, The Frail will always jump or appear head-first out of the same spot it entered.

* Unlike {{e|Peep}}, The Bloat's eyes are dislocated at the start of the fight.
** The {{e|Bloat Eye|text=Bloat's eyeballs}} float diagonally, bouncing off of walls, and do not take damage. They block Isaac's tears and inflict contact damage.
* Performs a small jump in place and fires eight projectiles in all directions.
** Unlike Peep's, The Bloat's projectiles are always shot in the same orientation.
* Creates large puddles of [[Creep#Red Creep|Red Creep]].
* Jumps into the air and travels a moderate distance in Isaac's direction, leaving a small puddle of Red Creep and sending out a ring of eight projectiles upon landing.
* Fires 2 {{i|Brimstone}} lasers from his eye sockets, aiming below him or to both sides of him, depending on Isaac's location. This attack is not telegraphed and fires near-instantly, although it can be deliberately triggered by standing beside or above The Bloat's head.
** He can not perform this attack upwards.
The Bloat deals a whole heart of contact damage.
sections.Notes: * The Bloat's eyes can be destroyed with {{p|Chaos Card}}, {{i|Euthanasia}}, {{i|God's Flesh}}, or {{i|Little Horn}}.

sections.Behavior:
Upon entering the boss room in {{s|Corpse}} II, the room is empty except for a hole in its center. Walking into it drops Isaac down into the arena where Mother is fought.

=== Phase 1 ===
Mother begins the fight attached to the top of the room and is stationary, similar to {{e|Mega Satan}}. Her face and hands can all be attacked to deal damage to her, and she uses them separately in her attacks:
* One of Mother's hands grabs a knife and throws it directly downwards. The knife emits projectiles horizontally while travelling and a burst of many projectile lines in a radius upon impacting the back wall. This attack has two variations in terms of the projectiles' paths.
* One of Mother's arms releases trails of projectiles that move across the arena in a wave pattern, eventually homing in on Isaac.
* One of Mother's hands slams the ground, releasing streams of projectiles in a radius and spawning {{e|Small Maggot}}s.
** Small Maggots that land on top of Mother's hitbox do not spawn.
* Occasionally, Mother spits out a unique {{e|Fistula}} at Isaac that bounces off walls. Mother swipes the Fistula towards Isaac whenever it travels close to one of her hands and releases 6 lines of 2 projectiles when it collides with the bottom wall. Mother repeats this several times, causing the Fistula to gradually gain speed, before slamming a hand down on the mass, crushing it and sending 3 medium Fistulas outwards. Each medium Fistula flies until it collides with a wall, sending out 2-3 small Fistulas and being destroyed in the process. These small Fistulas travel a short distance before bursting and spawning a Small Maggot.
** This Fistula can be reflected back towards Mother through the use of a variety of melee-based attacks, each reflect causing the Fistula to glow brighter. Successfully reflecting the Fistula 6 times will cause it to be destroyed upon contact with Mother, dealing damage to and briefly stunning her. It will also burst into 8 medium Fistulas in a radius that disappear quickly, six of which deal damage to Mother; each of these can also deal damage to Isaac. Abilities that can cause this interaction include:
*** {{i|Spirit Sword}}'s spin attack.
*** {{c|The Forgotten}}/{{c|Tainted Forgotten}}/{{P|Soul of the Forgotten}}'s bone swing.
*** {{c|Tainted Samson}}/{{P|Soul of Samson}}/{{i|Berserk!}}'s donkey jawbone swing.
*** {{I|Bag of Crafting}}'s swipe.
*** {{C|Tainted Magdalene}}'s hug attack, though it cannot be triggered by the Fistula.
* Occasionally, Mother retreats upwards, becoming invulnerable, and summons a horde of 34 {{e|Dead Isaac}}s at the bottom of the arena that walk up towards Mother. If any are left alive to reach Mother, she swipes with a hand, killing any that are caught in the swipe, releasing a tiny burst of red projectiles, and launching their corpses towards Isaac. After a while, she ends this attack by slamming down both hands, which causes a small rock wave to appear beneath any remaining Dead Isaacs, killing them, and launching their corpses up into the air.

=== Phase 2 ===
After losing 2222 HP, Mother retracts her head and arms into her body before releasing a green {{i|Mega Blast}} laser down the middle of the arena, destroying the lower wall and expanding the area of the room to be 1x2. She then separates from the top wall, launching her head into the center of the room. From this point on, she slides slowly towards Isaac when she isn't performing one of her attacks:
* Spins around in place, shooting out strings of wavy projectiles in all directions.
* Inhales and draws Isaac to her as projectiles appear behind Isaac as he moves. After that, she shoots a massive ball of projectiles towards Isaac that splits into many smaller clusters when hitting a wall, which each then send out lines of projectiles when they collide with a wall or Mother.
* Leaps upwards off-screen before charging vertically across the half of the room which Isaac is located within, then across the other half in the opposite direction. The half she charges across first is telegraphed by a splat at the top or bottom of the room. After this, she slams down in the middle of the room, sending rock waves and small strings of projectiles in all directions.
* Faint white lines appear at set intervals along a random arena wall before a line of projectiles quickly shoots out of the wall along each line; these projectiles hover for a moment before dropping. One line of projectiles is always lined up with Isaac's position. This attack is repeated five times and follows a pattern: vertical lines, then horizontal, vertical, horizontal, horizontal (or vice versa).

sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr+}} Using {{I|Plan C}} ''will'' kill Mother in time if you have an extra life. Even though Isaac dies well before the animation is complete, the [[Isaac's Last Will|game over screen]] will pop up almost immediately after the animation ends. If Isaac has an extra life item that revives him outside the room, he will be able to enter the Final Boss Chest without fighting Mother again.
** {{dlc|nr+}} Killing Mother in this way will ''not'' reward the completion mark for the current character if they don't have an extra life.
** {{dlc|nr+}} Killing Mother in this way will not work for {{c|The Lost}}, {{c|Tainted Lost}}, {{c|The Forgotten}} (if used as The Soul), and {{c|Tainted Forgotten}} if the revival transports them to the previous room since their death animations are shorter than those of normal characters.
* {{dlc|r+}} Using {{I|Plan C}} in Mother's room will now kill Isaac in 11.5 seconds, which is enough time to let Mother's death animation finish and reward the completion mark for the current character before [[Isaac's Last Will]] pops up.
* {{i|Rotten Tomato}} or any items that inflict [[Status Effects|Charm]] can cause Mother's wavy projectiles during the first phase and second phase to target herself.
* The ball of splitting projectiles in Mother's second phase can also collide with Mother. The player can therefore move to the opposite side of Mother after she fires to more easily dodge the attack.
* Unlike most other bosses, Mother has no visible health bar in either of her phases, so it is impossible to tell how much damage you are dealing to her without {{I|Spider Mod}}.
* {{I|Suplex!}} works on Mother, but in Mother's first phase, Isaac can pick up only one of her parts at a time, either her head or one of her arms, and give it a suplex.
* {{p|II - The High Priestess}} will damage Mother even though it can be considered another form of {{e|Mom}}.
* Using {{i|Black Hole}} will not stop Mother's wavy projectiles from proceeding once the black hole has diminished.
sections.Strategies:
* {{p|Chaos Card}} works on Mother, but only kills one of her phases. If you are holding a Chaos Card, it is recommended to use it in Phase 2, since Mother's attacks are much more dangerous.
* {{i|Curse of the Tower}} can be very useful, since {{e|Troll Bomb}}s will attempt to spawn near Mother, and bombs in ''Repentance'' will deal 100 damage and ignore the armor. Around 43 bombs would be able to kill her, which corresponds to about 6~7 times of damage. This will be affordable if you have more than 10 hearts in total.
** Similarly, using {{I|Anarchist Cookbook}}, {{p|XVI - The Tower}}, or your own {{e|Bomb}}s will also help.
* Her charging attack in Phase 2 can be greatly stalled by placing a bomb in front of her path, while also dealing damage to her in the process.
* In phase 2, if the player has {{I|Gnawed Leaf}}, they can bring Mother to a complete standstill while she's charging if they enter statue form in front of her.
** Pair this with at least one offensive familiar and the fight becomes a joke for all characters.
* Using {{p|Ace of Hearts}} during the Dead Isaac attack will spawn 10 hearts on average, which should keep any red heart characters alive for quite some time. Using it during the hand slam attack that spawns Small Maggots will usually spawn 3-5.
* Using {{I|Eraser}} on Mother's first phase allows phase 2 to be skipped as long she has 15 health or less.
* With proper timing, {{p|Soul of Judas}} can one-shot Mother's second phase even with base damage. The best attack for this is the spinning attack, but it is also possible to do this right after Mother spits out the ball of projectiles. Be aware that the boss can dodge the damage by performing the charge attack.

sections.Strategy: Throughout the majority of a run, Tainted Jacob is harassed by Dark Esau with no intended way of permanently getting rid of him. Because of this, playing as Tainted Jacob requires the player to manage both the playable Jacob and his vengeful brother Esau. * Using {{i|Anima Sola}} is key to success for Tainted Jacob, as it can help prevent damage from Dark Esau or turn him into a powerful weapon against enemies. * In the {{S|Mines}}, Tainted Jacob can intentionally run into Dark Esau in order to abuse the mechanics of The Lost form (specifically Flight in an area which normally removes any previous sources of flight you may have attained) to quickly and easily acquire the {{I|Knife Piece 2}} with a rapid and flight-assisted escape if you are attempting to reach the {{S|Corpse}} to defeat {{E|Mother}}. ** Typically, the escape path would become excessively difficult due to both {{E|Mother's Shadow}} and Dark Esau attempting to charge at you in intervals which are typically out of sync, making it very difficult to escape without taking damage or potentially dying. ** By remaining in The Lost form, this also allows you bypass the damage which would normally be required to enter the door in order to advance to {{S|Mausoleum}} / {{S|Gehenna}}. ** It is recommended to fully clear the floor first, as Tainted Jacob remains in The Lost form until the next floor is reached. * While in his Lost form, Tainted Jacob can take Devil Deals in the same way as the Lost. At the end of each floor with a Devil Deal spawn, it is possible to intentionally have Dark Esau turn Tainted Jacob into The Lost form in order to receive free Devil Deals. * Items and transformations that give you flight ({{tf|Guppy}}, {{tf|Beelzebub}}, {{tf|Seraphim}}, and {{tf|Leviathan}}) to be able to more easily dodge Dark Esau in rooms with pits and rocks, and/or spectral tears (quicker room clears with obstacles plus can cheese obstacle mechanics with Dark Esau) can help quickly clear rooms and avoid the brother's attacks. * {{t|Perfection}} is '''''not''''' lost upon getting hit by Dark Esau. * It can actually be quite risky to take {{i|Birthright}}. Each Dark Esau can charge in a different direction than the other, which ultimately increases your chances of getting hit by one of them. === Dark Esau === ===== Defense ===== Dark Esau himself should be respected. Being touched a single time by Dark Esau has a high chance of leading to a run's end by putting Jacob in his fragile Lost state for the remainder of a floor. * Dark Esau deals no contact damage to Jacob while chained down with Anima Sola. * Dark Esau's touch effect can be avoided while [[Temporary Buffs|shielded, invulnerable]], or otherwise immune to damage (such as with {{I|Holy Mantle}} or {{I|Gnawed Leaf}}). * Dark Esau keeps a consistent distance from Jacob, and will only charge if he is within this distance. Dark Esau will never actually be able to touch Jacob unless he starts his charge animation, charges, or Jacob runs into him. ** As such, running from and maintaining enough distance from Dark Esau will prevent him from charging. ** In some cases such as being next to an obstacle, Dark Esau will stop moving within the prop and will be unable to charge until Jacob moves away from it. ** Dark Esau will only charge at Jacob once he enters his cardinal line of sight. Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he is positioned diagonally from him, even if Jacob is standing still. * Dark Esau's position at all times is determined by his position relative to the general layout of the floor, meaning he persists in the same location even when Tainted Jacob moves through rooms. Entering a new room cancels Esau's charge if he was preparing one or frees him if he was bound by Anima Sola. ** Caution should be taken when moving between rooms where Dark Esau is near the doorway, as this may lead to a situation where Tainted Jacob immediately runs into Dark Esau. ** Teleporting a great distance or traveling quickly through rooms with the help of special items or a high speed stat makes it harder for Dark Esau to catch up to Jacob. ** If Dark Esau is in the process of traveling between rooms, it is possible to use Anima Sola to chain him outside of the current area Tainted Jacob is in. * As Dark Esau takes time to respawn after entering a new floor, the first few seconds on every floor can be used to explore rooms freely. * Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he eats a Paralysis [[Pills|Pill]]. ===== Offense ===== Considering the damage Dark Esau can deal to enemies and the fact that Anima Sola can be canceled early by using it a second time, Dark Esau can become a powerful, albeit dangerous weapon to use against enemies by positioning Tainted Jacob in ways that manipulate him into charging into enemies. This is further compounded, as his charge attack ignores [[Damage Scaling|Boss Armor]]. * Anima Sola can be used in an empty room to instantly summon Dark Esau in order to use him advantageously. ** Dark Esau's charge is able to single-handedly kill most early bosses in one or two hits. He can also be held in place with Anima Sola to bait chasing enemies, as Jacob can stand behind Dark Esau and cause them to run into him. * In [[Greed Mode]], Anima Sola will always be charged at the beginning of a new wave. This can be taken advantage of by binding Dark Esau before a new wave begins and then letting him charge into a freshly spawned enemy group or a priority enemy like a [[Monsters#Champions|champion]]. Since releasing Dark Esau manually does not consume the item charge, the item will still be available to restrict him again immediately afterwards. * Dark Esau's charge will extinguish {{e|Fire Place}}s. * Dark Esau cannot damage [[Status Effects|friendly]] enemies. * When Dark Esau charges while in [[Status Effects|fear]], he charges away from Tainted Jacob. ===== Co-Op Mode ===== * Dark Esau cannot affect other players and ignores them completely. ** {{dlc|nr+}} If multiple players are playing Tainted Jacob, then any Tainted Jacob who touches any Dark Esau will still be turned into a ghost or die. Tainted Jacob players will only be able to use Anima Sola on their own Dark Esau, and if one of the Tainted Jacobs is completely killed, both Dark Esaus will begin to target the one that is still living. ** {{dlc|nr+}} When Tainted Jacob completely dies and is turned into a small ghost baby as a Co-Op partner, Dark Esau will still follow the ghost of Tainted Jacob if no other Tainted Jacob players are in the match, allowing them to still use him as a high damage weapon to help their teammates. ** {{dlc|r+}} Dark Esau will no longer deal damage to enemies or charge at the ghost of Tainted Jacob until he is revived. * If Tainted Jacob was turned into his ghostly form by Dark Esau, then dying and being revived upon completion of the boss will have him revive as his ghostly form. ** {{dlc|nr+}} If Tainted Jacob is dead at the start of a floor, Dark Esau will still spawn, but will target one of the living players instead. Unless they are also playing Tainted Jacob, he will never hurt them outside his spawning animation. ** {{dlc|r+}} If Tainted Jacob is dead at the end of a floor, he will respawn at the start of the next floor. ===== Notes ===== * Dark Esau is considered a [[Bosses|boss]]. ** Like every other "boss", Dark Esau can be spawned with [[Debug Console|debug commands]]. However, if playing as someone other than Tainted Jacob, the player will be immune to his attacks. *** {{c|Jacob}}, even in his normal non-tainted form, is an exception. When touched by Dark Esau, he will take damage, but will not turn into a ghost. {{c|Esau}}, like most characters, is still immune to Dark Esau. * When the console command "restart 39" is loaded, the player will be spawned as a ghostly version of Tainted Jacob. The only differences is that Dark Esau never seems to spawn and that this version of Tainted Jacob has the health of {{c|The Lost}}.

* Spawns a {{e|Leaper}} into the air. It can land anywhere in the room while releasing its projectile attack immediately.
** There is a maximum of 4 Leapers alive at once.
** The Gate cannot perform other attacks if there are no Leapers alive. As such, it will also always perform this attack first.
* Shoots a ring of 9 projectiles that can rotate in either direction while expanding outwards.
* Shoots two rings of 6 projectiles which expand outwards and rotate in opposite directions.

** If faced alongside other enemies or bosses, such as in {{R|Boss Rush}}, the laser connects to them, damaging them as well.

sections.Behavior:
The Pile slowly slides around the room slowly and performs the following attacks:
* Burrows underground, then quickly reemerges elsewhere in the room and fires 5 bone projectiles in a spread towards Isaac. The Pile repeats this attack 3 times in a quick succession. It will generally try to reemerge close to Isaac or directly in his path to cut him off.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
Upon spawning, Reap Creep jumps up to the top of the [[Boss Room]] similarly to {{e|The Haunt}}. It starts off taking {{e|Wall Creep}}'s form and can perform the following attacks:
* Spawns a Wall Creep on either the left, right or bottom wall.
* Spews out a continuous stream of projectiles vertically while attempting to follow Isaac's movements.
** When reaching near the end of either wall, it leaves a gap between the stream and the wall.

=== Phase 2 ===
After losing 33% health, Reap Creep takes {{e|Blind Creep}}'s form and has new attacks:
* Spews a huge number of disorganized projectiles, similar to {{e|Monstro}}, but larger.
* Spews out a wide spread of spaced projectiles.
* Spawns 3-4 {{e|Spider}}s or a {{e|Trite}} downwards.

=== Phase 3 ===
After losing 66% health, Reap Creep takes {{e|Rage Creep}}'s form and has new attacks:
* Slams itself against either the left or right wall, causing rock projectiles and 3-4 Spiders to fall from the ceiling.
** If it's fought in the Mines, 3-4 {{e|Rock Spider}}s fall instead.
* Charges for a '''moderate''' period of time before shooting a wide {{i|Brimstone}} laser while attempting to follow Isaac's movements.
** When reaching near the end of either wall, it leaves a gap between the laser and the wall.
* Charges for a '''long''' period of time before shooting 4 regular Brimstone lasers diagonally outwards while attempting to follow Isaac's movements. The beams slowly come together leaving a small gap within the center.
** The two Brimstone attacks have distinct charge sounds, allowing the player to distinguish them.
sections.Notes:
* Reap Creep's arena always has a hollow upper layer, preventing Isaac from getting too close with it. This makes the situation tricky if Isaac somehow has to deal damage with melee or grounded attacks.
** Due to this, as of [[V1.06.J791]], Reap Creep cannot appear in the [[Scat Man]] challenge.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
The Matriarch hops randomly around the room and performs the following attacks:
* Spawns two small {{e|Fistula}}s once she takes 140 damage, and 2 more every 100 damage afterward.
** She takes considerable knockback when this occurs.
** {{dlc|r}} Reduced to 1 small Fistula for the first 2 spawns.
* Spawns a {{e|Fistuloid}} that chases Isaac, subsequently spawned Fistuloids orbit her. She can have up to a maximum of 4 spawned at once and does not spawn more until she has taken enough damage to release a small Fistula even if previous Fistuloids have been killed.
** Only 1 Fistuloid can chase Isaac at a time and they can occasionally swap when Isaac moves close to an orbiting Fistuloid. If the Fistuloid that chases Isaac is killed, one of the remaining ones stops orbiting the Matriarch and starts chasing Isaac.
*** The active chasing Fistuloid will not chase Isaac if he is too far away and returns to staying near the Matriarch until Isaac draws near.
*** Orbiting Fistuloids occasionally fire a projectile towards Isaac
** All Fistuloids spawned when there are 2 or more small Fistulas alive will orbit The Matriarch and one only becomes active when there is only one small Fistula left.
** {{dlc|r}} The Matriarch loses 30 HP each time she spawns a Fistuloid. If this would cause her to change phases or spawn small Fistulas, The Matriarch is unable to create Fistuloids.
* Jumps and launches 8 {{e|Chubber}} projectiles in all directions, which rebound back to herself.
* Spews a large long-range blood projectile towards Isaac that leaves [[Creep#Red Creep|Red Creep]] on the ground, similar to {{e|Mr. Fred}}.
** The puddle of Creep left at the end of the projectile's path lasts longer than the Creep trail.
** This projectile can kill the chasing Fistuloid.
The Matriarch's Chubber and regular projectiles deal a whole heart of damage.

=== Phase 2 ===
After taking 340 damage, the Matriarch rapidly spawns waves of glowing red Fistuloids that have 20 HP and quickly lose health, causing them to shoot their maggots almost immediately.

=== Phase 3 ===
After taking enough damage, the Matriarch repeats the phase transition attack from Phase 1 to 2. During the rest of this phase The Matriarch no longer spawns Fistuloids and only uses the Chubber and projectile attacks.

=== Phase 4 ===
When at low HP (after taking ~540 damage), The Matriarch's shell splits into a medium-sized Fistula, 2 small Fistulas and a Fistuloid, and she turns into a low HP {{e|Chub}}.
* Previously orbiting Fistuloids, including the one spawned, permanently orbit her Chub form, while previously active Fistuloids continue to chase Isaac.
* The Matriarch as Chub always spawns charging in a random direction, regardless of Isaac's position, before returning to the normal Chub pattern, similar to the {{e|Charger}}s spawned by {{e|Sloth}}.
* If the Matriarch eats a {{e|Bomb}} during her charge attack, she spits it back out at Isaac.
** Most bomb modifiers will still be present on the bomb, except for {{i|Bomber Boy}}.
sections.Notes:
* {{Dlc|r}} The Matriarch is unique in being twice as common than other [[Boss Room]] Bosses in the Scarred Womb boss pool, but only 1/4th as common as other Boss Room bosses in The Womb.
** This makes her the only boss in the game to have a boss weight higher than 1 on any floor.
** This also makes her the only boss to have a special weight which isn't an alternative variant of another boss on the same floor.

sections.Behavior:
Rag Man chases Isaac if there are no {{e|Rag Man's Ragling}}s alive and can stop to perform the following attacks:
* Throws his head towards Isaac. The head rolls for a bit, after which it turns into a Rag Man's Ragling. His head then reappears on his body. While his head is rolling, his body walks around aimlessly, occasionally shooting a homing projectile in a random direction, behaving similar to a {{e|Gusher}}.
** The head has 25 HP and can be shot to damage both Rag Man and the Ragling spawned from it.
** Rag Man's Raglings leave remains on the ground after death. If the head is destroyed before transforming, it still creates a Ragling's remains.
** Rag Man can only spawn up to 4 Raglings.
** If there are any Rag Man's Raglings alive, Rag Man switches from chasing Isaac to following one of his Raglings.
* Revives all nearby Raglings from their remains and heals himself for 10 HP during the process, regardless of the number of Raglings resurrected.
** By doing this, he can overheal above his original HP amount of 200.
* Fires 1, 3, or 5 homing projectiles at Isaac in quick succession.
Once Rag Man is killed, his Raglings' remains disappear, and the Raglings that are still alive won't leave remains upon death.
* {{dlc|r}} Raglings that are still alive will instantly die once Rag Man is killed even if they were not originally spawned by Rag Man himself.
** However, they will not die if they're in their spawning/head stage when Rag Man was killed.
sections.Notes:
* Rag Man will often be accompanied by his own Raglings at the start of the battle, but they aren't able to leave remains upon death.
* He can also start surrounded by 8 spiders.
* The health bar of Rag Man will flash orange for a short time to indicate that he is healing.
* Killing Rag Man's spawned Raglings with {{i|Lusty Blood|n}} doesn't boost Isaac's damage.
* Rag Man's head can be caught using the {{i|Friendly Ball|n}}.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
Sisters Vis perform the following attacks in conjunction:
* Similar to {{e|The Cage}}, Sisters Vis curl up into balls and roll around the room, bouncing off the walls and each other. One of them leaves a trail of [[Creep#Green Creep|green creep]] and begins rolling towards Isaac while the other leaves behind a trail of [[Creep#Brown Creep|brown creep]] and begins rolling away from Isaac. After a while, one sister stops rolling before the other and:
** Fires a {{i|Mega Blast|n}} laser in the cardinal direction closest to Isaac's position.
*** This Mega Blast laser occasionally sweeps back and forth in a wide arc.
** Fire 2-4 lines of 3-5 projectiles in the cardinal direction closest to Isaac's position.
The attacking Sister Vis finishes a few seconds before the other Sister Vis stops rolling.
* The sisters leap into the air and land on each side of Isaac's position either vertically or horizontally. They then fire Mega Blast lasers towards each other. The two beams collide and stop in the middle of the sisters.
* Together they spawn either two {{e|Vis}} or two {{e|Begotten}}s.
** These spawns can be killed if caught in their rolling or their Mega Blast attacks.
* If only one sister is targeted and ends up taking a lot more damage compared to the other in a short period of time, then the sister not being targeted becomes enraged for the rest of the fight, attacking and moving at a faster pace.

=== Phase 2 ===
When one of the two is killed, the other becomes enraged.
* She no longer performs the jump attack but always performs a Mega Blast or projectile attack after rolling.
* If the Sister Vis that leaves Green Creep dies first, the other will leave Green Creep instead of Brown Creep.
sections.Notes:

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
The Fallen moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:
* Fires 3 projectiles in a spread followed by 4 projectiles in a spread in succession towards Isaac.
* Increases its speed and chases Isaac. After taking a certain amount of damage, it halts and fires a {{i|Brimstone}} laser in each cardinal direction.

* At 50% health, The Fallen splits into two smaller versions of itself. The two clones have identical behaviour.

sections.Notes:

sections.Behavior:
Pin burrows into the ground before performing the following attacks:
* Jumps out of the ground towards Isaac and burrowing back into the ground at the end of the jump.
** {{dlc|nr}} Occasionally fires 4 projectiles diagonally from the last section of its body when exiting the ground and/or when burrowing back into the ground.
** {{dlc|r}} Fires 4 projectiles diagonally depending on the length of its jump: does not fire projectiles on short jumps, fires projectiles shortly upon exiting the jump on regular/medium jumps, and fires projectiles both shortly upon exiting and after a few moments airborne on long jumps.
* Partially emerges out of the ground to fire a red {{i|Ipecac}} shot at Isaac before returning underground.
** After performing this attack, Pin will always jump out of the same spot it entered.
sections.Notes:
* Each segment of Pin can be individually damaged, so a single piercing tear could hit Pin multiple times.
** Moreover, if Pin is petrified (due to {{i|Mom's Contacts}} or {{i|Charged Baby}}, etc.), his individual segments can even be destroyed (though that would not necessarily deal higher damage), which will shorten the boss in its length.[[File:Shorter Pin.png|thumb|Pin with several of his segments destroyed, appearing much shorter.]]
** {{Dlc|r}}Piercing shots no longer damage segmented enemies multiple times per attack.
* Despite looking like it's flying above the ground, Pin is not immune to ground-based effects such as [[creep]] when doing its jumping attack. On the contrary, every segment is guaranteed to pass over the damaging area, making it more susceptible to damage.
** Due to this, Pin also cannot jump across gaps, and will bounce backwards when attempting to cross one.
* The segment that shoots bullets during mid-jump will continue to do so if it's suspended in mid-air with something like {{I|Anima Sola}}.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
The first phase occurs against Rotgut's "face" in its regular boss room. Rotgut is stationary in the center of the room and performs the following attacks:
* Spews a constant wave of projectiles that alternates above and below it in a fanning pattern.
* Spews out waves of fluctuating spaced-out projectiles in a disorganized pattern.
* Fires rings of 8 expanding projectiles that alternate between rotating clockwise and counter-clockwise.
* Fires three waves of projectiles in a row:
** A radial of tightly knit slow-moving tears.
** A radial of spaced out fast-moving tears.
** A burst of randomly positioned tears that hover for a moment before dropping.
* Coughs up a horizontal burst of red projectiles to the left and right side of itself.
* Vomits out projectiles, bones, as well as {{e|Globin}} goo, {{e|Gazing Globin}} goo, and {{e|Small Maggot}}s that rain down in a large area.

=== Phase 2 ===
Once Rotgut's first form has been defeated, it sucks Isaac, any monsters, and floating projectiles into its mouth and sends Isaac into a {{r|Crawl Space}}-like interior. The second phase consists of a large maggot that sits in the bottom right of the room and performs attacks depending on Isaac's position.

If Isaac is on the platform, the maggot uses its rear end:
* Launches a cluster of projectiles onto the platform and covers it in green poisonous gas.
* Launches an {{i|Ipecac}} shot that bursts into arcing tears.
* Shoots out 6 slow travelling tears that travel in a wave pattern across the entire room.

If Isaac is below the platform and on the ground, the maggot uses its head:
* Spits out a stream of arcing blood projectiles along with a few {{e|Attack Fly|text=Attack Flies}} and Small Maggots.
* Shoots out a {{i|Brimstone}} laser.

=== Phase 3 ===
Defeating the Maggot allows passage into the next chamber, which contains Rotgut's "heart". The heart switches randomly between two modes of projectile patterns that occur for the entire duration of the fight:
* Mode 1: shoots out half-rings of 6-7 green projectiles below it with each pulse of the heart.
* Mode 2: drops 3 yellow projectiles in random locations with each beat of the heart. Each projectile splits into 2 arcing projectiles after hitting the ground.

The heart can perform additional attacks that occur independently of its two set modes:
* Retreats upwards and spawns {{e|Leech||Leeches}} on the end of the room furthest from Isaac. These Leeches move quickly across the screen and despawn upon reaching the edge of the screen. The final Leech spawned has a chance of being an {{e|Adult Leech}}.
* Drops 2 large blood projectiles below it one after another. Each bursts into smaller projectiles that bounce all over the room.
After defeating this phase, Isaac is automatically ejected out of Rotgut's insides and back into the boss room.
sections.Notes:
* Dying with a respawn item (such as {{i|Dead Cat}}) in the second or final phase places Isaac in the previous phase, meaning Isaac has to fight that phase again. This does not apply to effects that revive the player in the same room such as {{i|Inner Child}}.
* The transitions between phases count as room changes (which means the {{i|Holy Mantle}} shield will re-activate after each phase, for instance).
* The chambers for second and third phases are not considered boss rooms for the purposes of items such as {{i|Blanket}}.
* {{i|Vanishing Twin}} will spawn a copy of Rotgut's first phase. When either of them is defeated, the fight can be advanced to second phase without killing the remaining boss. Second and third phases are not affected except for the fact that Vanishing Twin familiar will remain with Isaac despite having transformed into a copy of Rotgut. After Isaac defeats the third phase of the boss, the familiar will spawn another Rotgut, which will instantly die and drop an item.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
The Lamb floats towards Isaac and performs the following attacks:
* Fires 6 rings of 10 projectiles outwards with one projectile always aimed in Isaac's direction. The Lamb continues to move towards Isaac but at a very slow pace while performing this attack.
* Shoots rotating waves of 3 projectiles around himself in all directions that split apart once they make contact with any surface, similar to {{i|The Parasite}}.
* Fires 5 rotating lines of projectiles.
** The Lamb occasionally spawns 0-3 {{e|Attack Fly|text=Attack Flies}} during any of the 3 attacks above.
* Fires 2-4 lines of homing projectiles in a spread that rotate to follow Isaac's movements.
* Unleashes a burst of many small {{i|Ipecac}}-like projectiles in random directions.

=== Phase 2 ===
Once The Lamb reaches 50% HP, his body detaches from his head and falls to the ground. This phase has each part of The Lamb attacking independently of each other.

The head of The Lamb continues to chase Isaac and can still perform most of the attacks from Phase 1. He loses the explosive shot attack and no longer spawns Attack Flies but gains 3 additional attacks:
* Charges extremely quickly directly towards Isaac, stopping at the edge of the room.
* Stops in place and fires four {{i|Brimstone}} beams in the cardinal directions. The beams can rotate 90 degrees either clockwise or counterclockwise.
* Fires a large burst of homing projectiles towards Isaac, similar to the combination of {{i|Monstro's Lung}} and {{i|Spoon Bender}}.
* Defeating the body first has no effect on the head's behavior.

The body of the Lamb remains stationary at the position the Lamb was at the end of Phase 1. The body has one attack which it performs at random intervals but while the head is attacking:
* Fires a large burst of disorganized projectiles in all directions and spawns up to 5 Attack Flies.
** If the head is defeated first, the body can spawn up to 25 Attack Flies.
* When the body is killed, a {{cu|darkness}} effect is applied for a long period of time.

sections.Behavior:
Unlike the other Ultra Harbingers, Ultra Death has only one phase and has three attacks which he cycles through indefinitely:
* Summons a rectangle of 11 {{e|Ultra Death Scythe}}s which close in towards Ultra Death's position and continue in the same direction until disappearing off screen. Ultra Death uses this attack 3 times in a succession.
* Flies off screen, then reappears travelling slowly while summoning waves of {{e|Ultra Death Head}}s which move up and down across the screen in the same direction. At the end of the attack, the skulls freeze in place and Ultra Death summons three harmless scythes which spin outwards, destroying the skulls.
* Immediately after the previous attack, the screen darkens and Ultra Death disappears into the darkness. Ultra Death appears next to Isaac and swings his Scythe before disappearing again, darkening the screen with each attack. This attack is repeated 4 times, afterwards, the screen returns to normal and Ultra Death reappears.
** His position during this attack can be indicated by a faint glowing red eye.

Ultra Greed is fought in a unique vertical double-size room with golden Boss Room doors on all 4 walls in regular positions.
When Isaac enters the boss room, Ultra Greed starts out hanging on a noose before he abruptly cuts it off and lands on the ground. Ultra Greed cannot be damaged until he drops to the ground. Ultra Greed then performs a variety of attacks in addition to wandering around the room:
* Stomps on the ground 4 times, spawning a {{e|Keeper}} with each stomp. Only 4 Keepers can be alive at once.
* Charges at Isaac when he is in line of sight.
* Shoots either 3-5 coin projectiles in a spread from his mouth, or a cluster of coin projectiles, similar to {{e|Monstro}}.
** Ultra Greed does not perform this attack if Isaac is far enough away.
* Spins around the room, firing coin projectiles in random directions.
* If Isaac is too close to Ultra Greed, he performs a spin, kicking Isaac away in the process.
* Stops moving and rotates his eyes in a slot machine manner. If both eyes land on the same symbol, he then spawns multiple [[Ultra Greed Coin]]s of the same symbol.
** If the two symbols on Ultra Greed's eyes don't match, he spawns {{e|Ultra Greed Coin (Spinner)||Ultra Greed Coins (Spinner)}}.
{{entity table | Ultra Greed Coin (Spinner), Ultra Greed Coin (Key), Ultra Greed Coin (Bomb), Ultra Greed Coin (Heart) }}

* If there are too many monsters/coins alive at once, Ultra Greed assumes a defensive stance. While blocking, Ultra Greed takes much less damage from Isaac's attacks, and maintains this state until most of the monsters/coins have been killed.

All of Ultra Greed's attacks deal a full heart of damage and cause Isaac to drop coins on hit. If he walks over any coins on the ground, he collects them, healing him for 4.375 HP each. Doing so also makes him slightly more aggressive. Heart coins also make the boss angrier.

When Ultra Greed has low health, he turns red, which increases his attack speed and movement speed. This effect also occurs if Ultra Greed is healed by enough Heart Ultra Greed Coins, although only providing a temporary effect.
* The scaling speed increases if {{a|Everything is Terrible 2!!!}} has been unlocked by using the {{e|Greed Donation Machine}}.

When Ultra Greed's health bar is depleted, he turns into a golden statue and drops the end chest and the {{e|Greed Donation Machine}}. If in [[Greedier Mode]], he instead begins his second phase.
{{clear}}
sections.Notes:
* After Key Coins appear, using {{p|A Card Against Humanity}} causes spawned Gapers to be stuck and, as long as they're alive, Ultra Greed will not attack.
* Having {{i|E. Coli}} (and perhaps other contact-based collectibles) is a fast way of disabling the Bomb, Key, or Heart Coins because they don't do contact damage. However, unmarked coins do.
* {{dlc|a+nr}} Except for direct contact and the {{i|Brimstone}} lasers, all of Ultra Greedier's attacks only do explosive damage. Therefore having {{i|Pyromaniac}} or {{i|Host Hat}} makes this phase of the fight much easier to survive.
** {{dlc|r}} The rock waves after Ultra Greedier's jump attack are no longer considered explosive damage.
* {{dlc|a+}} The entire room will be turned to gold when he dies. This is due to a special shader that turns on in the room when he dies, so using effects like {{P|A Card Against Humanity}} or {{p|XVI - The Tower?}} will make the grid entities spawned look golden.
* Any poop spawned in the Ultra Greedier fight, destroyed or not, will respawn as {{g|Golden Poop}} when Ultra Greedier dies and turns the room into gold.
** {{dlc|r}} This effect is only visual, they act like regular {{g|Poop}} when destroyed despite the gold color.
* If you manage to spawn a {{e|Sticky Nickel}} (possibly through a {{i|D20}}) Ultra Greed may station himself over it and no longer move around the arena.
* {{I|Eraser}} can allow the Ultra Greedier phase to be skipped if you use it on Ultra Greed when he has 15 or less HP.

sections.Behavior:
The Rainmaker floats slowly towards Isaac and performs the following attacks:
* Creates two horizontal lines of 6 projectiles each on both sides of himself, then fires them towards Isaac at intervals starting from the far ends towards the center.
* Creates a ring of 12 projectiles around himself, then fires them towards Isaac in short staggered intervals starting from 2 opposite ends of the ring.
* Summons a large water projectile overhead, then pops it, unleashing a burst of projectiles in random directions.
* Twirls around, following Isaac's movements while summoning projectiles around himself which hover briefly before being fired towards Isaac.
** At the end of this attack, the Rainmaker releases 8 projectiles in a radial burst.
The Rainmaker deals a whole heart of contact damage.
sections.Notes: * The Rainmaker can be immediately killed with {{I|Vade Retro}} if he is at 50% health or below.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
* Charges either left or right off-screen and continuing on from the opposite end of the screen. Continues until he has crossed the screen three times.
** He performs this attack more often if Isaac is to his left or right.
* Shoots eight projectiles in all directions.
* Ascends off-screen and summons 5 {{e|Troll Bomb}}s.

Once his health is below half, War's horse blows up, dropping War, who performs a crying animation.
* War charges quickly at Isaac gradually building speed and making more tighter turns.
** Every time War loses around 1/3rd of his remaining HP in this phase, he pauses briefly to sob before restarting this process.
War deals a whole heart of contact damage in both phases and during his charge.

sections.Behavior:
The Stain burrows underground when Isaac is not within range. While burrowed it becomes invincible and follows Isaac's movements. When close to Isaac, it pops out and performs one of the following attacks:
* Sends out 2 patterns of numerous projectiles in all directions. The first barrage consists of fast-moving bullets that slow down. The second barrage consists of slow-moving bullets that speed up.
* Sends out tendrils to its left and right leaving small puddles of damaging [[Creep#Red Creep|Red Creep]] directly around The Stain and to its either side.
* Spawns 2 {{e|Charger}}s and can have a maximum of 3.
It will stay vulnerable for a brief moment after performing an attack before quickly burrowing underground again.

Tuff Twins always spawn in a pair consisting of 5 body segments and a head segment each. They are always fought in a double-sized room.
* The Tuff Twins roam around the room randomly, like {{e|Larry Jr.}}
* The Tuff Twins are initially covered in rock armor that gives them immunity to all non-explosive damage, but bombs and explosives can destroy their armor, making their segments vulnerable to all damage.
** There are always at least two {{e|Bomb Grimace}}s that dispense {{e|Throwable Bomb}}s for Isaac to use against the Tuff Twins to break their armor.
** All segments have damage resistance to explosives both before and after having their armor removed, taking only 25-14% damage based on how far away the explosion is from them.
*** This also applies to Isaac's tears if they have an explosive effect, such as if he has {{i|Ipecac}}, {{i|Dr. Fetus}}, etc.
** The armor absorbs up to 15 damage before breaking, and is independent of the segments' 35 HP value.
* Head segments occasionally spit {{e|Ink}}s while protected by its rock armor.
** Vulnerable head segments spit {{e|Sucker}}s instead.
** Head segments will not try to spawn Inks or Suckers if there are at least 4 total in the room. However, head segments can occasionally spawn multiple in succession, bypassing this limit.
* Vulnerable body segments spew bloody shots, similar to {{e|Boil}}s.
* Tuff Twin segments can be split into smaller copies of the boss as long as the new Tuff Twin segments are longer than 2 pieces.
* The Tuff Twins become faster the more rock armor they lose.
sections.Notes:
* {{i|Terra}}, along with any items that create rock waves like {{i|Mega Bean}} and {{i|Wait What?}} can destroy the Tuff Twins' armor.
** {{dlc|r+}} {{p|Hagalaz}} will also remove their armor on use.
* {{i|Sulfuric Acid}} tears cannot destroy their armor. 
* Destroying all the {{e|Bomb Grimace}}s with effects like {{i|Little Horn}} and {{i|Euthanasia}} and then somehow wasting all of the bombs they drop when destroyed can soft-lock Isaac in this fight.
* {{I|Plan C}} cannot kill the Tuff Twins if they still have their armor.

sections.Behavior:
The Wretched's behavior is similar to {{e|Widow}}'s: making large leaps towards Isaac, and can perform the following attacks after landing:
* Leaves a puddle of [[Creep#White|White Creep]] that is slightly larger than Widow's, and shoots 8 white projectiles outwards.
* Spits out 2 {{e|Spider}}s, a {{e|Big Spider}}, or a {{e|Trite}}.
** The Wretched can kill her own summons if she jumps on top of them.
* {{dlc|r}} Spawns 3 Spiders upon death.

The Scourge floats quickly around the room, attempting to get above Isaac's position. It can perform the following attacks:
* Shoots a large, fast cluster projectile out of its hood that homes in slightly on Isaac. When it hits a wall, it explodes into a spray of projectiles, leaving behind damaging [[Creep#Green Creep|Green Creep]] and a cluster of {{e|Small Maggot}}s.
** If The Scourge is below half health, it instead shoots out three slower, smaller cluster projectiles from out of its hood that create fewer projectiles on impact.
* Launches one of its tendrils towards Isaac and embeds it in a wall. It then drags the tendril along the wall, causing projectiles, creep, and Small Maggots to shoot out from the wall.
* Launches two tendrils and embeds them into the wall, one directly at Isaac and one in the cardinal/ordinal direction opposite of him. It then starts rotating its arms around while shooting two rings of 12 projectiles outwards.
* Launches two tendrils to either side of Isaac, embedding them into the wall and trapping him in a triangle-shaped area. It will then perform one of two attacks:
** Fires walls of tight projectiles with gaps to pass through from its body. It follows up each wave with an additional, faster projectile aimed directly at Isaac.
** Fires horizontally travelling projectiles randomly out from both its left and right tendrils.
** If Isaac gets caught out of this triangle space for any reason, The Scourge will cancel this attack.
*** The three previous attacks end if The Scourge or its tendrils take enough damage. Each tendril has a total HP of 400.
*** The Scourge takes damage equal to 25% of the damage its tendrils take.
*** The tendrils passively take heavy damage if they're dragged along a wall, dealing a total of 50 damage to The Scourge for each tendril dragged.
*** The tendrils kill Small Maggots they are dragged into.
* Moves to the center of the room and begins sucking in 2 tight streams of projectiles towards it in a spiral pattern. This spiral pattern can randomly switch directions during the attack. Additional random projectiles can appear in the gap between the two streams, further limiting the space.
sections.Notes: * The Scourge is instantly killed by {{I|Meat Cleaver}}.

sections.Behavior:
* If Isaac has any [[familiar]]s, The Siren sings, charming up to 3 familiars at a time to assist her and turning their effects against Isaac.
** Isaac's familiars when charmed retain most of their behaviors when assisting The Siren but can now deal contact damage and block shots.
** Charmed familiars have 60 HP and return to Isaac when killed.
* If she has less than 3 charmed shooting familiars from Isaac, she summons up to 3 orbiting {{e|Siren Minion}}s of her own. These familiars behave identically to {{i|Brother Bobby}} but with a slower fire rate and can also be killed. She then glides around the room for a few seconds, letting her familiars use their effects against Isaac. If she has any familiars alive after this, she swipes at Isaac, launching all remaining familiars in a cluster in his direction.
** When the cluster collides with a wall it kills all the familiars and releases a burst of radial projectiles and a cluster of disorganized projectiles.
*** The amount of projectiles launched during this attack depends on the number of familiars that collided with the wall.
* Swipes a short distance in Isaac's direction, releasing 5 projectiles.
* Sinks into the floor becoming invulnerable and chases Isaac, leaving a trail of slowing [[Creep#Black Creep|black creep]]. After reappearing, she swipes at Isaac, shooting a spread of 5 projectiles.
* Screams, emitting a consistent shockwave around her and spawning 9 pulsating rings of projectiles that expand outwards.
** This attack pushes Isaac away like an inverted {{e|Gaping Maw}}.
** The rings of projectiles have openings towards Isaac's general direction.

Upon death, The Siren burns away, leaving behind her skull.
sections.Notes:
* Bombing the skull that the Siren leaves behind spawns and unlocks the {{t|Forgotten Lullaby}}.
** It only spawns the {{t|Forgotten Lullaby}} the first time it is bombed.
** Bombing the skull in subsequent runs treats it as a regular [[Rocks#Skulls|Skull]] in regards to its drops.
** Leaving and returning to the room causes the skull to disappear.
* {{dlc|nr+}} The Siren can charm {{C|Lilith}}'s [[Familiar]]s, including her {{I|Incubus}}, hence making Lilith a difficult character to kill The Siren with. To counter this, either bait The Siren into launching the familiars into the wall and killing them or use bombs/active items to deal damage.
* {{dlc|nr+}} Charmed familiars with a charged attack (eg: {{i|Lil Brimstone}}) hold their charge until the Siren launches the familiars.
* {{dlc|nr+}} Lasers from charmed {{I|Robo-Baby}} and {{i|Robo-Baby 2.0}} do not hurt Isaac.
* {{dlc|nr+}} Charmed {{i|Lil Portal}} can still collect pickups and create a portal.
** {{dlc|r+}} Charmed Lil Portal does nothing and has no hitbox.
* Charmed familiars that are thrown (eg: {{i|Bob's Brain}}) do not count towards the count of 3 familiars that orbit the Siren but are included in the cluster thrown at the end of the attack.
* Charmed {{i|Abel}} mirrors The Siren's movements and shoots at her, though these projectiles are dangerous towards Isaac and do not hurt The Siren.
* Charmed {{i|Paschal Candle}} will still grant a tears buff while charmed.
* Charmed {{i|Rotten Baby}} spawns {{e|Attack Fly|text=Attack Flies}} instead of Blue Flies and {{i|Sissy Longlegs}} spawns {{e|Spider}}s instead of Blue Spiders.
* Charmed {{i|Tinytoma}} orbits The Siren but still blocks hostile projectiles and turns into friendly Blue Spiders after being destroyed. It will also not return to Isaac when destroyed and will spawn charmed again for The Siren.
* Temporary familiars and {{i|King Baby}} cannot be charmed.
* Charmed [[knife Piece 1|knife familiar]] cannot be damaged while it returns after a stab.
* Charmed {{i|Angelic Prism}} will still split tears and deal contact damage to the character, but it wont work for the enemy.
* Charmed {{i|The Peeper}} / familiar from {{i|The Scooper}} will still have the effect of increasing eye damage. The creep from {{i|The Scooper}} will damage enemies.
sections.Unlockable Achievements: {{achievement text | Forgotten Lullaby }}

sections.Behavior:
Widow makes large leaps towards Isaac, at approximately double the distance of {{e|Monstro}}, and can perform the following attacks after landing:
* Leaves a puddle of [[Creep#White|White Creep]] and spawns a {{e|Sack}}.
** There is a maximum of 3 Sacks alive at once.
* Spits out a {{e|Spider}}.
* Widow can kill her own Spiders and Sacks if she jumps on top of them.

Ultra War.infobox:
{{infobox boss | dlc = r | name = Ultra War | portrait = no | id = 951 | variant = 30 | environment = Boss
{{floor|Home}} | base hp = 2000 | pool = ''None'' }} '''Ultra War''' is a [[boss]] added in ''[[The Binding of Isaac: Repentance]]'' and is the third of the [[Harbingers (Bosses)#Ultra Harbingers|Ultra Harbingers]] fought before {{e|The Beast}} in {{s|Home}}.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
Ultra War charges in from the side of the screen and has two attacks which he alternates between:
* Throws a large, {{e|Giga Bomb}} that deals contact-damage and explodes mid-air in a cross pattern that spreads across the entire screen, similar to {{i|Bomber Boy}} Bombs. The Bomb also releases a burst of 12 lines of 4 projectiles outward when it explodes. This attack is repeated 3 times.
* Charges off-screen, then wraps around the bottom of the screen 3 times, creating 4 to 6 pillars of harmless light in alternating positions across the screen, from which large lava projectiles launch upwards with staggered timing.

=== Phase 2 ===
Ultra War dismounts from his hobby-horse and has two new attacks which it alternates between:
* Chases Isaac, then lunges diagonally downwards in Isaac's direction. After, Ultra War releases 4 streams of fire in the cardinal directions as well as a small burst of slower moving fires in all directions. This attack is repeated 2 times.
* Lunges diagonally downwards while holding a large bomb which explodes in a cross pattern that spreads across the entire screen. Ultra War then bounces across the sides of the screen 3 times while moving upwards before plummeting into the lava below. When Ultra War emerges, he creates 4 to 6 large lava projectiles that launch upwards with staggered timing.

* Upon death, Ultra War explodes, which can damage Isaac at close range.
sections.Notes:
* If Isaac has the {{t|Safety Scissors}}, the Giga Bombs Ultra War throws will be defused and fail to explode, after which they can be picked up or left to fall into the lava.
* Ultra War's Giga Bombs can be killed by {{i|Euthanasia}} shots.
* The lava projectiles can be slowed and knocked down with certain slowing items such as {{I|Censer}} and high knockback tears.

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
The Visage is bound together by a chain and cannot be damaged; the chain must first be destroyed to progress the fight, and has 150 HP. During this phase, it only has one attack:
* The heart slowly wanders around the room, and the mask attempts to move toward Isaac, constrained by the length of its chain (which reaches up to 4 tiles outward). Occasionally, the mask charges at Isaac when he approaches it from any cardinal direction, predicting his movements. Upon colliding with a wall, the mask launches out a spray of rock projectiles before being pulled back to the heart.
** The mask cannot charge if it’s close to Isaac.
** The chain only extends for this attack, it's normally rigid and constrains the mask and the heart to a specific length.
** If the mask hasn’t charged in a while, it starts pulling the heart with it in its attempt to reach Isaac.

=== Phase 2 ===
Once the chain is broken, the mask and heart are unbound from each other and their behavior changes:
* The mask freely moves around the room, briefly speeding up and chasing Isaac if it sees him in a cardinal direction.
** The mask has 100 HP, and can be damaged by explosions, piercing shots, or by being shot in its open back. Upon death it deactivates, which stops it from moving, dealing contact damage to Isaac, or from firing certain projectiles when used by the heart. However, it can still block Isaac's tears.
* The heart now actively avoids Isaac, but also uses a chain to perform a variety of attacks in conjunction with the mask:
** Launches a chain to the mask. Once attached, it directly pulls the mask in and fires a horizontal helix of {{i|Brimstone}} lasers that pushes both backwards into a wall.
*** The lasers and pushback don’t happen if the mask is deactivated.
** Launches a chain to the mask. Once attached, it swings the mask around in a spiral while also bringing the two closer. The mask fires red projectiles outward while being reeled in. If the mask collides with wall before it unites with the heart, it creates rock projectiles on impact and is then pulled directly to the heart.
*** The mask doesn’t fire projectiles while being reeled in if it’s deactivated.
** Launches a chain to the mask. Once attached, it directly pulls the mask in and then jumps onto Isaac's position, creating a burst of rock projectiles as well as 4 rock waves in the diagonal directions upon landing.
** Launches a chain at Isaac. If the chain hits him, it pulls him into the heart, causing him to take contact damage. If the chain misses, it pulls the heart into the wall it hits, creating a burst of rocks and red projectiles. This attack can only be used if the mask is deactivated, and takes higher priority once it becomes available.
*** Unlike all other attacks, the chain directly hitting Isaac doesn’t deal damage, only him being pulled into the heart does.
*** If the chain hits a bomb while being launched, the bomb instantly explodes and the attack is cancelled.

=== Phase 3 ===
When the heart drops to half HP, its visual outer shell breaks, exposing the heart. The Heart's movement becomes quicker and more erratic along with an attack change:
* Launches a large, slow-moving energy ball known as {{e|Visage Plasma}} in a diagonal direction that bounces off of walls. If this projectile touches the mask, it fires a {{i|Brimstone}} laser out its back, rapidly propelling it in the direction it was facing and creating rock projectiles and a radial burst of 8 projectiles upon collision with a wall.
** If the mask is deactivated, Visage Plasma will automatically travel towards it, reviving it as well as causing its normal effect.
** Visage Plasma have 50 HP, and can be destroyed by Isaac.
** The heart always begins the phase with this attack.
* Briefly stops moving and fires out a ring of 16 red projectiles.
* If there are 3 Visage Plasma floating around the room, the heart sucks them in, drawing in Isaac in the process. Each Visage Plasma absorbed heals the heart a small portion of HP. After absorbing all 3, it fires out 4 tight rings of fire along with 4 short-range diagonal {{i|Brimstone}} lasers.
** The mask deactivates during this attack, regardless of its HP. Unless the heart is on a far side of the room and Isaac is far away enough, Isaac must hide behind the mask to dodge this attack, as the rings of fire are too dense to weave through.
Once the heart has been killed, the mask permanently deactivates.
sections.Notes: * The Visage's deactivated mask can be still targeted by effects such as {{i|Anima Sola}}.

sections.Behavior:
Ultra Pride differs from its normal counterparts by having attacks more similar to {{e|Super Sloth}} and a {{e|Baby}} than {{e|Pride}}. They perform attacks independently of each other.

Edmund wanders randomly around the room and performs one of two attacks:
* Shoots out 3 arcing homing projectiles.
* Throws out a horizontal line of [[Creep#Green Creep|Green Creep]] if Isaac is to his left or right.
** The line is cone-shaped and will always be wider to the right end, no matter which direction it was sent from.
Ultra Pride Edmund deals a whole heart of contact damage.

Florian slowly floats towards Isaac and can randomly teleport around the room.
* If Isaac is close, he periodically shoots out a homing projectile that deals one full heart of damage.
* Florian has {{dlc|nr}} 25 HP / {{dlc|r}} 30 HP.
sections.Notes:
* If Edmund is defeated last, Ultra Pride drops {{t|The Left Hand}}, regardless of whether or not it has already appeared during that run. If this is the first time it is defeated, the Left Hand [[achievement]] is also unlocked.
* If Florian is defeated last, there is a 25% chance to spawn {{dlc|nr}} a [[Treasure Room (Item Pool)|A Treasure Room]] item / {{dlc|r}} the {{i|Eternal D6|n}} if it has been unlocked.
* {{dlc|nr}} Florian is treated as an ordinary {{e|Baby}} by the game, so it still has a chance to spawn as an {{e|Angelic Baby}}. This will override its unique appearance.
* {{dlc|a}} In one room, two Edmunds can spawn instead of one of each.
sections.Unlockable Achievements: {{achievement text | The Left Hand }}

sections.Behavior:
=== Phase 1 ===
Turdlet consists of 5 separate segments that travel together similar to {{e|Larry Jr.}}, and acts the following way.
* Moves around the room loosely chasing Isaac, making wide turns and bouncing on walls.
* After 7 seconds of normal movement, huddles its body together, then launches tail-first towards Isaac while straightening out. Its head end spins around its tail while bouncing against walls at high speeds before eventually decelerating to a full stop.
* Turdlet leaves a trail of slippery [[Creep#Brown Creep|Brown Creep]] wherever it moves.

=== Phase 2 ===
* After dropping to 30 health or less, Turdlet splits into two parts with two segments, each continuing the same behavior.
** The health each split Turdlet has is equal to the health the original Turdlet had when it split, plus 15.
** While both parts are alive they coordinate the launch attack by huddling together.
sections.Notes:
* Using the {{i|Meat Cleaver}} on Turdlet instantly skips its first phase.
* Since the health Turdlet's split segments have scales depending on how much health the original Turdlet have when it split, if a strong attack (like a {{e|Bomb}} or {{p|II - The High Priestess}}) causes Turdlet to split, its split segments will have significantly less health.

sections.Behavior:
The Turdlings spawn as a pair and wander around the room. Each individual Turdling has one attack in total which is performed independently of the other:
* Rushes towards Isaac when aligned in any cardinal direction, leaving behind slippery [[Creep#Brown Creep|Brown Creep]] until it has run into a wall.
** After rushing into a wall, it spawns 4 {{e|Brownie Corn}}s that launch out in the cardinal directions.
** Occasionally, after rushing into a wall it will fart, knocking back Isaac and nearby Brownie Corns.
** Its dash can be interrupted if it runs into a Brownie Corn.
sections.Notes:
* {{Dlc|r}} The Turdlings are much less common than their counterparts, spawning only 1/4th as often.
* {{dlc+|r+}} {{i|Flush!}} kills Turdlings instantly and causes them to leave behind 6 {{e|Dip}}s each.{{dlc-}}

sections.Behavior:
* Wrath wanders around the room randomly, occasionally standing still.
* Throws a {{E|Bomb}} towards Isaac if he is in line of sight and then attempts to run away from the bomb.
** Wrath takes only 20 damage (as opposed to the usual {{dlc|nr}} 60 / {{dlc|r}} 100) from his own bombs.
Wrath deals a full heart of damage (both bombs and contact).
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|anr}} Occasionally, 2 regular Wraths appear in a Mini-Boss Room and the boss message will display "Isaac vs {{E|Super Wrath}}".
* Isaac's bombs and {{i|Epic Fetus}} missiles deal 200 damage to Wrath regardless of modifiers or damage stat.
* {{dlc|nr}} Wrath can drop {{i|Mr. Boom}} even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.
sections.Unlockable Achievements: {{achievement text | The Book of Sin }}
